## Detailed Design

### Core Rules

**Conventions.** Rule ids are `MSA-n`, collision-free across `design/gdd/`. Formulas are `D.n` in this document; a formula owned elsewhere is always prefixed with its owner (`LSG D.14` is the Graph's seam formula, `LY D.6` Layout's weld offset). Acceptance criteria are `AC-MSA-nn` and are pre-assigned below (the Acceptance Criteria section expands each to Given/When/Then and keeps these ids). Diagnostics are `MSA_*`. Assembly's reason codes are namespaced `MSA.<CODE>` under the kernel's `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)`. Every new number carries `[PLACEHOLDER]` and a registry-candidate line (see *Names this GDD introduces*, end of this section). Neighbour rules are cited by rule id (`LS-15`, `LY-16`, `BDY-24`, `IA-14`), never by line number, because sibling GDDs are still being edited. "Advisor R<n>" names an orchestrator ruling that decided the point; "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" names a reconciliation made while authoring. Each rule gives **Rule**, **Criterion** (AC ids), **Pillar**, an *Alternative considered* line where a choice was made, and *Decides*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* One tag is added: `[VS-B]` marks a co-op rule, target or criterion (it needs a second seat, a MIRROR client or a crewmate's presence) and is excluded from the MVP gate; the one-weld-versus-three-verbs contingency is stated once, in the Overview. Every paragraph, row or criterion changed by the first design review carries "*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*". No fault rule relies on an exception being thrown or caught: GDScript has none (MSA-31).

#### A. Shape of the system

**MSA-1 — Five commands, three families.** *Rule:* Assembly registers exactly five command types (table T1). **Family W (weld):** `begin_weld` (PLAYER, CHANNEL) and `weld` (SYSTEM, the atomic completion). **Family C (seam cut):** `begin_seam_cut` (PLAYER, CHANNEL) and `seam_cut` (SYSTEM, the atomic completion). **Family I (install):** `install_module` (PLAYER, TAP). The `begin_*` commands open a channel and mutate no ship state; the completions are the atomic cross-block applies; install is a one-shot atomic apply. No other type is registered. `remove_module` is reserved and unregistered (MSA-28). The name `begin_cut` is Interaction's V8 module salvage and is never used here; `CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` and `SALVAGE_*` are likewise never reused. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-01. *Pillar:* P5, anti-pillar "not a freeform builder" (three pre-shaped verbs). *Decides:* advisor R1, R4, R5, R10, R27.

**T1 — Command types** (registry: `assembly_commands`).

| Command | Origin | Mode | Payload (primitives only) | Actor binding | Coalesce | `max_age_ticks` | Declared / registered | Reason set |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `begin_weld` | PLAYER | CHANNEL | `{target_ref}` (a `WELD_SOCKET` subject in `FREE`) | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | `MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION` 120 (kernel, cited) | Interaction declares the row (IA-23); Assembly registers | `weld_ready`, IMMEDIATE half (T2); tool `tool_welder` |
| `begin_seam_cut` | PLAYER | CHANNEL | `{target_ref}` (a `WELD_SOCKET` subject in `WELDED`) | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | 120 | declaration row requested of Interaction (ASK I1); Assembly registers | `seam_cut_ready`, IMMEDIATE half; tool `tool_cutter`; `CUT_BLOCKED` |
| `weld` | SYSTEM | atomic completion | `{actor, socket_a, socket_b, cause}`, `cause` = `CHANNEL` | explicit `actor` field (SYSTEM origin has no issuer binding) | `NONE` | `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` 12 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (MSA-6) | Assembly | `weld_ready` full; DEFERRED branch resolves to `BLOCKED` |
| `seam_cut` | SYSTEM | atomic completion | `{actor, seam_id, cause}`, `cause` in {`CHANNEL`, `CASCADE`} | explicit `actor` field | `NONE` | `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` 12 | Assembly | `can_detach` set, `CUT_BLOCKED` |
| `install_module` | PLAYER | TAP | `{hardpoint_ref}` | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | 120 | declaration row requested of Interaction (ASK I1); Assembly registers | IMMEDIATE set only; DEFERRED branch resolves to `BLOCKED` |

All reasons are computed from true state and the kernel never filters them (CR-5). `allowed_origins` of `weld` and `seam_cut` is SYSTEM only (a channel completion or a cascade); tests submit them through a SYSTEM-origin double.

**MSA-2 — Assembly owns decisions, not mutations.** *Rule:* Assembly owns the five commands, the weld quality `q`, the channel durations, the offer predicates, the cut-mode derivation, the order of mutator calls inside each apply, `assembly.state`, `assembly.step`, and its reason codes. It owns no geometry (Layout), no seam edges, atmosphere or the formulas `cap_seam`, `hp_seam`, `A_seam_m` (Graph), no pose, velocity or actors (Body), no item vocabulary (Item DB), and no channel clock, abort set, partial-progress ledger or noise (Interaction). Every state change goes through a mutator the owning system publishes (kernel CR-9; H1, H3). Assembly writes exactly one block, its own. It adds no arithmetic of its own to the Graph's seam formulas: it supplies `q` and `L_seam` and cites `LSG D.14` and `LSG D.2` (D.4 below works them at MVP values). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-02 (review: no restated foreign arithmetic or value), AC-MSA-03 (lint: the only block Assembly writes is `assembly.state`; every other write is a published mutator). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* advisor R2; KRN H1, H3.

**MSA-3 — Weld and seam cut are two-phase: begin, accrue, handoff, completion.** *Rule:*

1. **Begin (P2 of tick `Tb`, PLAYER).** `begin_weld {target_ref}` or `begin_seam_cut {target_ref}`. `validate` runs the IMMEDIATE half of the predicate only (MSA-7, MSA-8). `apply` calls Interaction's proposed Class B `open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks)` and the Controller's `set_channel_ref(actor, ASSEMBLY, channel_id, face_octant)` (published, PC-1 b; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*), where `face_octant = octant_of(anchor_o(target_ref) − foot)` is computed in this apply (Controller D.8: the octant whose D.3 `UNIT` vector maximises the integer dot product, ties to the smaller index; `NONE` only for a zero vector), `anchor_o` being the interaction anchor of the `target_ref` subject (the `WELD_SOCKET` subject for `begin_weld`, the seam subject for `begin_seam_cut`, the same anchor Interaction's `in_reach` uses) and `foot` the actor's `pos_curr`, both in the actor's body frame; the Controller stores it as `channel_face` and locks facing to it for the channel *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, CONFLICT)*; the apply mutates no ship state. Coalesce `NONE`.
2. **Accrue (P3, Interaction).** `interaction.step` runs the clock, the shared abort set, the lit recheck, the partial-progress ledger and the noise exactly as for its own verbs (MSA-30). Per IA-14, elapsed `e = T - Tb` and accrual happens at `e = 1..D`, so a fresh channel is DONE on the P3 of tick `Tb + D` (a channel resumed from the ledger is DONE `resume_offset` ticks sooner; the arithmetic below is for a fresh one).
3. **Handoff (P3 of tick `Tb + D`, `assembly.step`, ordered after `interaction.step`).** It reads the DONE handoff Interaction exposes in `channel_view` and re-runs the IMMEDIATE predicate. On a fail it writes `last_result = REJECTED(reason)` and submits nothing (the channel's cost is spent; the cause is world-visible). On a pass it writes `pending {kind, target_ref, submit_T}` and submits the SYSTEM-origin completion `weld {actor, socket_a, socket_b, cause CHANNEL}` or `seam_cut {actor, seam_id, cause CHANNEL}`.
4. **Completion (P2 of tick `Tb + D + 1`).** Authority, then `validate` proves everything by pure reads (MSA-7, MSA-14, MSA-20), then `apply` is total.

*Worked example (cited convention, weld at the Save/Load registry's tick):* a weld begins in P2 of `Tb` = 437039; accrual happens on ticks 437040..437399 (`D` = 360); the DONE handoff is in P3 of 437399; the completion applies in P2 of 437400. Because both channel durations are multiples of `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 (IA-14 lint), the channel spans a whole number of 6-tick blocks, but DONE need not fall on a Graph hook tick. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-04. *Pillar:* P1 (a state change during a six-second channel is re-validated, never assumed), P3. *Alternative considered:* a one-phase shape in which the hook calls M2/LM2/BM3 directly at channel end — rejected: the hook would skip `validate`, and "both verdicts must pass before apply" (Layout's `socket_plan` contract and its Interactions row) would have no home, so a defect would become FAULTED instead of a clean reject; a `begin_*` that is itself the command applied at press with the channel as a wind-up — rejected: the world would change before the work. *Decides:* advisor R10; KRN CR-9; LS-15 ("`can_join` is run at the command's `validate`, the same tick as apply").

*Origin caveat (load-bearing).* Hooks may submit SYSTEM-origin commands only (KRN CR-3), so every channel-completed `weld` and `seam_cut` reaches P2 as SYSTEM. Body's BDY-24 keys the hatch-cap rule on origin ("PLAYER-origin cut rejects, SYSTEM-origin cut defers"). This GDD reads that split as **`cause`**: a `CHANNEL` completion **rejects** with `CUT_BLOCKED` (at begin, at handoff and at completion); a `CASCADE` completion **defers** (MSA-22). The wording refresh is routed to the Body owner (CONFLICT C7).

**MSA-4 — `assembly.state` holds outcomes only: no progress, no history.** *Rule:* block id `assembly.state`; class `SIM`; `persist true`; `persist_scope WORLD`; scope `SHARED` with per-seat records keyed by **PlayerId** (never the transport peer id); `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY`; `schema_version 1`; `restore_after [layout.state, graph.state, interaction.state, body.state]`. Per seat it holds `pending {kind NONE|WELD|SEAM_CUT, target_ref, submit_T}` and `last_result {verb_id, target_ref, outcome, reason, T}`; the `[VS]`-reserved CASCADE deferral record (MSA-22) is the only other field. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **`last_result` is runtime-only.** It is the presenter's input (MSA-34, D.17), not world state: it is outside `snapshot()`, outside the canonical bytes of every hash scope and outside the Save/Load payload, and it is still carried in the `SHARED_SUMMARY` replica. A restore therefore leaves it empty by construction, with no clearing step, and the save-equivalence test (MSA-38, AC-MSA-61) is not defeated by a field that every restore resets. Alternative considered: keep `last_result` persisted and list it as a permitted difference in AC-MSA-61 and S7 — rejected, because after the first `DONE` the hash of a restored run would then differ from the uninterrupted run at almost every later tick, which turns the main equivalence test into a test of nothing. Kernel ASK K3 asks the kernel owner to confirm that a block may declare a field runtime-only in `snapshot()`; ADR candidate "assembly.state persistence".)* Schema in table T6. It stores **no channel progress** (that is Interaction's record, MSA-30) and **no world history** (that is Layout's `welds[]`: `welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`, state). `snapshot()` writes every seat's `pending` as the NONE record, so `post_restore` clears nothing: it runs the verifier on the as-restored block (the `pending` clause of INV-10 is then vacuous, MSA-32) and the block is restore-idempotent, the Controller's PC-17 pattern *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(orchestrator ruling, QA-lead flag F-10; **Amended 2026-10-27 — design review**: the earlier text said a snapshot in the handoff window still has the weld target `FREE` or the cut seam `WELDED`. **MSA-5 — One hook, `assembly.step`, with two jobs.** *Rule:* `(hook_id assembly.step, owner Assembly, divisor 1, offset 0, after [interaction.step])`. It does exactly two things: (a) turn a DONE ASSEMBLY handoff into the completion command (MSA-3.3); (b) resolve a completion that was Rejected or Dropped by the TTL rule (MSA-6). It submits SYSTEM-origin commands only and writes only `assembly.state`. It iterates seats in ascending PlayerId, reads only `channel_view` and its own block, submits at most one SYSTEM command per seat per tick, and uses no wall-clock, no RNG and no dictionary-order dependence, so the same state always submits the same commands (what makes replay and MIRROR identity possible). It is O(seats <= 4) reads when idle. Divisor 1 because the handoff must follow DONE on the same tick. `interaction.step` must never name `assembly.step` in its own `after` (no cycle); an unknown `interaction.step` id fails boot (CR-3). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-07 (auto: deterministic output, ascending PlayerId, hook-order registered), AC-MSA-62 (lint/budget, MSA-39). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* advisor R2, R10, R12; TD-11.

**MSA-6 — The completion carries nothing derived; its life is bounded so `DONE` and `NOT_TAKEN` are mutually exclusive.** *Rule:* the completion payload is exactly `{actor, target, cause}` (target = the socket pair or `seam_id`): no `q`, no plan, no mode. `q` is read from the knob at apply, the plan is re-derived from Layout's `socket_plan`, the mode is derived (MSA-19). A payload that carries nothing derived stays replayable and gives a hallucination nothing to influence. `assembly.step` stores `submit_T` in `pending` when it submits. The completion's `apply` clears `pending` and writes `DONE` or `BLOCKED`. If `pending` is still set when `T - submit_T > PENDING_TTL_TICKS`, `assembly.step` writes the neutral outcome `NOT_TAKEN` and clears it (the true reason goes to the result event for DIAGNOSTIC and replay only; there is no reason text for the player). The two registered completion types set `max_age_ticks = PENDING_TTL_TICKS`.

*Why that makes the two outcomes exclusive by construction.* A hook-submitted command is stamped `queued_tick = submit_T`. At P2 of tick `submit_T + k` its age is `k`, and the kernel rejects `STALE` when age exceeds `max_age_ticks`. So the command can apply only while `k <= PENDING_TTL_TICKS`; at `k = PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1` P2 rejects it `STALE` and the P3 of that same tick (after P2) is the first tick on which `T - submit_T > PENDING_TTL_TICKS` and `assembly.step` may write `NOT_TAKEN`. No late `Applied` can follow a `NOT_TAKEN`, and no `NOT_TAKEN` precedes an apply. Constraint (formula D.11): `PENDING_TTL_TICKS >= ceil(QUEUE_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK)` = 8, which is the kernel's own never-stale invariant (`KRN D.7`: `max_age_ticks(any type) >= 8`), so a local command is never spuriously stale from queue depth; default 12, range 8-119 `[PLACEHOLDER]`. **One guarantee, the BUSY gate** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `pending.kind != NONE` is a `BUSY` term at site 1 only (MSA-7), so a `begin_*` pressed while a completion is unresolved is refused at the prompt rather than queued behind it; this, not a duration floor, is what makes it impossible for a new handoff to meet an unresolved `pending` (a resumed channel can be as short as 6 ticks, D.7, so a floor on channel length proves nothing). The range tops out at 119 because of clause 2 (`MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION` 120 minus 1). A rejection at admission (`QUEUE_FULL`) or in P2 leaves `pending` set, so the same TTL covers it; the cue arrives `PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1` = 13 ticks (about 0.22 s) after submission, which is acceptable for a neutral cue. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: in that window the pending target may already be `WELDED` (a rival completion applied first, E-7, AC-MSA-59) or the seam already `CUT`. That is legal, `pending` does not assert anything about the target's state, and INV-10 accepts it (T7); what `pending` does until the TTL is gate a new `begin_*` (`BUSY` at site 1) and hold the cue back to `submit_T + 13`. The lifetime of `pending` is therefore "`submit_T` until the apply clears it or the TTL fires", and MSA-4, E-30, E-33, MSA-33 and MSA-38 say so.)* *(orchestrator ruling: supersedes the wording of advisor R12, which wrote `NOT_TAKEN` when `pending` was "uncleared at T+1". Under the kernel's `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` truncation a legitimate completion can apply at T+2..T+8, so R12's wording could write `NOT_TAKEN` and then `DONE` for the same weld. The outcome name, neutrality and clearing behaviour of R12 are kept; only the trigger is TTL-based. The specialist proposal `MSA_COMPLETION_MAX_AGE_TICKS` 2 is rejected: it violates the kernel's `max_age_ticks >= 8` boot invariant.)* A sim hook has no confirmed path to command result events (CR-10: simulation systems never subscribe), so the rule reads only `assembly.state`, as Interaction's own door retry reads its `attempts[]`; whether a hook can read a result event at all, and the `issuer_peer` of hook-submitted commands, are ASKs to the kernel owner (ASK K1). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-08 (auto: under an injected backlog of 1..8 ticks the result is `DONE` exactly once and `NOT_TAKEN` never; a completion rejected at admission yields `NOT_TAKEN` at `submit_T + PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1`), AC-MSA-09 (lint: payload fields; `max_age_ticks == PENDING_TTL_TICKS`; value within 8-119). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* TD-6, TD-7, F-TD-1; advisor R10, R12; KRN CR-5, CR-13, CR-17, `KRN D.7`.

**MSA-8 — IMMEDIATE reasons reject; DEFERRED reasons are outcomes after cost.** *Rule:* a reason is **IMMEDIATE** iff it depends only on geometry, light, the actor's own state, tool or stock, registry structure, pose or the consequence channel. IMMEDIATE reasons reject at the `begin_*` commands and are shown in the world (a missing prompt or the standard rejection cue). A reason is **DEFERRED** iff it depends on module-body state (`hp`, `state`, `forced_mode`, `served_pm`, a node being ABSENT, DESTROYED or SALVAGED). Two exist: `PORT_ABSENT` (weld) and `SLOT_OCCUPIED` (install). A DEFERRED reason is **never read by a PLAYER-origin `validate`** (MSA-9). In a completion `apply`, step A0 re-runs the full Graph `can_join` (weld) or `check_install_module` (install), SYSTEM-side. If the only failing verdict is DEFERRED, `apply` writes `last_result = BLOCKED(reason)`, clears `pending` and **mutates nothing else** (M2 or M5 is never called); both branches of `apply` are total, an Applied command with an outcome, not a fault, following the IA-12 / IA-24 precedent. The structural half (`can_join_static`) runs first in `validate`, so a DEFERRED verdict can never mask a structural failure (`PORT_ABSENT` precedes later structural reasons in the Graph's own order; a masked read would be lossy). Two non-home bodies `[VS]` tie-break on the lower `body_id`; several mates `[VS]` tie-break on the lowest `(socket_key_a, socket_key_b)` (formula D.3). MVP has exactly one pair: `sock_airlock_e` (home-ship, facing E) and `sock_b_w` (derelict B, facing W), `class_id` 1 (`SOCKET_CLASS` = DOCK_STD), `width_tiles` 2, lanes POWER lane 0 and O₂ lane 0, no COOLANT lane, one hatch each, weld offset `(696, 384)`. Assembly repeats the lane set and the offset as Derelict Authoring's must-repeat asks (DA-10). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-15. *Pillar:* P5 (the home-ship body survives). *Decides:* advisor R14; LY-16.

**MSA-12 — The player weld is offered only once the pair is docked.** *Rule:* `weld_offer(seat, socket)` is a pure read published by Assembly (formula D.2) and is the `eligible` predicate of Interaction's `begin_weld` declaration row: it is true iff the welder is the equipped tool, the seat is `lit` and `in_reach` of the socket, the socket is `FREE`, a unique mate passes `can_attach`, and `docked(a, b, frame_shift_px)` holds. No prompt exists unless the offer holds. `NOT_DOCKED` exists only as a backstop (T2). Web Map & Transit establishes `docked` (WM-21 `berth`; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: no longer provisional*); Body tests it; Assembly gates the *offer*, as BDY-27 asks ("the offer, not Body's `validate`, is gated"), so the player never sees "the ship jerking". Four consequences. (1) `weld_offer` reads only tool, light, reach, Layout socket state and Body `docked`; it never calls `can_join_static` or the full `can_join`, never reads a node or edge accessor and never reads `surge[]`, and it is a hot-path read (cached static half, O(1) `docked`; its per-call budget is `MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US`, a placeholder in T9 whose value the spike sets). (2) `eligible` currently has one member, `actor_sane_gate` (IA-2), so adding `weld_offer` is an ASK to Interaction; the dependency runs Interaction -> Assembly read view while Assembly calls Interaction's mutators, so it is an injected read-view lookup, not a code import -> ADR candidate. (3) The channel lasts 360 ticks, so Transit could separate a pair during it: the mitigation order is (i) ASK to Transit — do not break `docked` for a pair while an ASSEMBLY weld channel is open on it (readable from `channel_view`) *(answered: WM-22 holds `docked` and makes `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` `BUSY` while an ASSEMBLY channel is open; Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (ii) the handoff pre-check re-tests `docked` (T2a), which closes all but one tick. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: Body's open request is accepted and the former fallback (iii) is deleted: the Pipeline's `BODY_TRANSFER` camera cut hides camera motion, not the exterior hull jump (BDY-27), so the offer never drops the `docked` term; `docked` is a hard term of the offer, closed by (i) and (ii).)* *(orchestrator ruling: the technical-director's option B, re-checking `docked` in the completion `validate`, is rejected because Body's locked text says weld legality takes no pose input; the handoff re-check is not a kernel `validate`, so it does not contradict it.)* (4) The visual cursor is Layout-supplied data drawn in world space (UI Requirements). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-16 (auto: offer false when not docked, no prompt), AC-MSA-17 (lint + spike: `weld_offer` source calls no `can_join*` or node accessor and meets its budget). *Pillar:* P1. *Alternative considered:* not gating and relying on the camera cut — kept as the named fallback only. *Decides:* advisor R17; BDY-27; TD-8, TD-16.

**MSA-13 — `q` is a data constant: never an input, never displayed.** *Rule:* `q = WELD_Q_DEFAULT` 850 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, loaded from the data file, range **`Q_MIN`(`LEAK_HP`) to 990, stated once in D.1** (400 to 990 at the default `LEAK_HP` 4000) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: every other mention of the range in this GDD cites D.1 instead of restating it)*, default 850 *(refines advisor R11, which ruled 400-1000: LSG D.2's floor form gives `A_seam_m` 0 from birth only at `q` of 993 or more, and 0 once `leak_bp` is low enough, and the Graph's own `SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP` row calls "welds never weep" an R9 violation, so q 1000 would delete the weld's P1 tell)*. There is no player input, no modifier slot and no `Σ q_mods` term anywhere in the rules; the Vertical Slice options (a hold-longer trade, a weld-rod part) appear in Open Questions only, because a modifier slot in the rules invites progression creep. `q` goes into the plan handed to `weld_join` and the Graph stores it on the SeamRecord. `q` is never shown in any prompt, preview, tooltip or player-visible debug HUD; the Debug Overlay reads the true value. Its consequences are physical and come from the Graph, cited and never restated as Assembly's: `cap_seam` is 925 permille of the lesser port at q 850, `hp_seam` is 8500 (above `HP_OK` 7000), `leak_bp` starts at `SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP` 10000 unscaled, and the D.2 seam area `A_seam_m` gives the weep (`LSG D.14`, `LSG D.2`; worked in D.4). **Named cliffs for the knob.** Below 400, `hp_seam = q * 10` falls below `LEAK_HP` 4000 and every MVP weld would start leaking at birth, which breaks P2 fairness (a leak with no prior tell); data outside the range is clamped at **both** ends, to `Q_MIN` (400 at the default `LEAK_HP`) or to 990, and logged `MSA_Q_CLAMPED`. **The upper cliff is q of 993 or more** (q = 1000 is the limiting case, LSG D.2 Output Range): `A_seam_m` is 0 from birth, the seam has no weep, and the weld's own P1 tell vanishes; at q 990 (`Q_MAX`) the fresh seam still weeps, at 2 milli flow units, for about 6.3 minutes (worked in D.1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **The lower cliff is q < 400**, named above. Default 850 keeps the Graph's q-dependent paths exercised only at one value in play; the Graph side tests q 400 and 1000. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-18 (lint: clamp and diagnostic), AC-MSA-19 (lint: `q` reaches no player-visible string or UI path), AC-MSA-20 (review: no modifier term). *Pillar:* P1, anti-progression. *Alternative considered:* `q` from hold time, a consumed weld rod or tool condition — rejected for MVP (channel length would become player-variable, no such Item DB def exists, tools have no durability). *Decides:* advisor R11; `LSG D.14`.

**MSA-14 — The weld `apply` runs in one fixed order; every call has a named proof.** *Rule:* after the completion's `validate` passes and the A0 deferred check is clear, `apply` runs in this order (table T3): Graph M2 `weld_join(plan)` -> Layout LM2 `attach_section(socket_a, socket_b, seam_id, welded_at_T)` -> Body BM3 `rebase_on_attach(surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, frame_shift_px)` -> Interaction `sync_section(section_a)` and `sync_section(section_b)` -> `assembly.state` (clear `pending`, write `last_result = DONE`). The order Graph -> Layout -> Body is Body's (BDY-21): BM3 or BM4 before its Layout mutator is `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, a defect. Assembly allocates no id; the `seam_id` that LM2 needs is returned by M2 *(answered 2026-10-27: Graph LS-15, `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`; Layout Open Question 4 closed; Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and without that return the chain cannot be written (fallback: Assembly allocates, which advisor R6 rejects on H3 grounds). The apply is infallible *by proof*, not by hope: each call's precondition is a pure read already run in `validate`, and a call with no proving read is a FAULTED path and a design defect (TD-1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **fault detection is explicit, because GDScript has no throw and no catch.** A runtime error ends the function with a default return and the caller carries on; `assert()` is compiled out of a release export. "Infallible by proof" therefore needs a detector that does not depend on either. The contract (MSA-31): every Class A mutator Assembly calls (M2, LM2, BM3 for a weld; M3, LM3, BM4 for a cut; M5 for an install) returns a status, `OK` or a `FAULT_CODE` naming the violated precondition; Assembly's `apply` checks the status after **every** call, and on the first non-`OK` it calls `ctx.fault(code, detail)` (kernel CR-19(a), ASK K2 answered *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) and returns `ctx.complete()` at once, making no further mutator call. A mutator that returns `OK` but leaves a cross-block disagreement is caught by the release postconditions of MSA-32 (INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5 and INV-7 after each weld or cut) and by the always-on integer comparisons `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT` (A3 against A4) and `MSA_VERDICT_DRIFT` (A0 against V4), which are promoted from debug assertions to release-fatal faults.)* One P5 notification batch results, with the Graph's keys `T`, `S/<seam_id>`, `SEC/<a>`, `SEC/<b>` (and nothing else from the Graph) plus Layout's `BODY/` and `SEC/` keys for moved sections and Body's keys. Weld `apply` is integer arithmetic only: no RNG, no wall-clock (H9). The Graph's keyed draws (`rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no << 20) | subject_id)`) are unchanged by a weld or a cut because a weld only appends ids and never renumbers (LS-9, LS-15), so replay identity across a weld needs no Assembly term. Budget: M2 alone <= 0.2 ms Release (locked, Graph); the whole weld `apply` is a placeholder budget measured in the spike (Tuning Knobs). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-21 (auto: recorded call trace equals the T3 order; a BM call before its Layout call raises `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`), AC-MSA-22 (auto: exact P5 batch keys), AC-MSA-23 (spike: budget), AC-MSA-24 (auto: a table-driven test enumerates T3 and asserts every apply call has a proof entry), AC-MSA-142 and AC-MSA-143 (auto: a mutator returning a `FAULT_CODE`, and a half-applied A3, each fault the kernel in a release-configured build) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Pillar:* P1 (the world is never half-welded). *Decides:* advisor R6, R10; KRN CR-9; BDY-21.

**T3 — Weld apply ledger.**

| # | Phase | Call | Owner / class | Proof (pure read in `validate`, or total by contract) | Data in -> out | If the proof were wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | validate | kernel authority (SYSTEM allowed; explicit `actor`) | Kernel | CR-5 | -> | `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, Rejected |
| V2 | validate | `can_attach(socket_a, socket_b)` | Layout, pure | Layout's eight reasons | sockets -> verdict | Rejected `VALIDATION_FAILED(layout.<REASON>)` (LY-29); owner reasons keep their owner's namespace |
| V3 | validate | `socket_plan(a, b)`; add `q := WELD_Q_DEFAULT` | Layout, pure | returns `{pairs[], openings[], L_seam}` | -> plan | Rejected |
| V4 | validate | `can_join_static(plan)` | Graph, pure | nine structural reasons | plan -> verdict | Rejected |
| V5 | validate | `can_rebase_attach(surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, frame_shift_px)` (Body's published arity, BM3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | Body, pure | `BDY_REBASE_SAME_BODY`, `BDY_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY` and `BDY_REBASE_SHIFT_OFF_GRID` (a published reason) | -> OK | Rejected with Body's reason in Body's namespace |
| A0 | apply | full `can_join(plan)`: compare structural verdict with V4 (`MSA_VERDICT_DRIFT`); read `PORT_ABSENT` | Graph, pure | same-slot guarantee (CR-2, CR-9) | -> deferred? | defect: `MSA_VERDICT_DRIFT` faults the kernel (release too) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| A1 | apply | **if `PORT_ABSENT`**: `last_result = BLOCKED(PORT_ABSENT)`, clear `pending`, return | own block | total | -> | none; the one "applied but did nothing" branch |
| A2 | apply | M2 `weld_join(plan)` | Graph, Class A | V4 + A0 (full `can_join OK` is M2's own precondition) | plan -> `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}` *(answered, LS-15; Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | FAULTED |
| A3 | apply | LM2 `attach_section(socket_a, socket_b, seam_id, welded_at_T)` | Layout, Class A | V2 plus the `seam_id` from A2 | -> `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}` | FAULTED |

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

21	## Overview
22	
23	**Modular Ship Assembly is the system that changes the shape of the ship: it owns the three player commands that weld a derelict section onto the home-ship, cut a welded section away along its seam, and seat a carried module into a hardpoint, plus the one number of workmanship (`q`) that colours every weld.** At the data layer it is a thin orchestrator over four other owners' state. Assembly owns no geometry (Layout), no seam edges or atmosphere (Graph), no pose or actors (Body), no item vocabulary (Item DB), no channel clock or noise (Interaction). 24	
25	The player meets Assembly as a physical act, never as a menu. Docked beside a dead ship's airlock, lit and holding a welder, they hold `E · Weld` for six seconds, standing still while the web may be listening; a four-pixel Hull Grey bead appears across the frame and two hulls become one body. Nothing else happens: a weld moves nothing, the hatch is still shut, the valves still closed, the breaker still open, and the seam weeps faintly through the area the Graph gives it. Making the graft live is the player's own later work (open the hatch, open the valve, close the breaker, each a lit Interaction verb with its own physical answer). With the cutter they can later cut the section away along that same seam, clean if they prepared it and ragged (a breach on both sides) if they did not; the cut leaves a cap plate or a ragged scar that never goes away. Carrying a salvaged scrubber or heater home, one press seats it into a pre-shaped hardpoint with a clunk, and the machine either turns or does not. The bead, the cap plate, the scar and the seated module are the player's visible history on the ship; none of them is ever a number.
26	
27	Without this system the game's first promise has no verb: "a body they assembled from the corpses of other ships" is a sentence, derelict sections could only be stripped and abandoned, a salvaged module would have nowhere to go, and Pillar 5 (salvage integrates into the body that survives; scarcity pushes inward; loss costs ship and body, never knowledge) would have no ship-shaped record to point at. 131	### Core Rules
132	
133	**Conventions.** Rule ids are `MSA-n`, collision-free across `design/gdd/`. Formulas are `D.n` in this document; a formula owned elsewhere is always prefixed with its owner (`LSG D.14` is the Graph's seam formula, `LY D.6` Layout's weld offset). Acceptance criteria are `AC-MSA-nn` and are pre-assigned below (the Acceptance Criteria section expands each to Given/When/Then and keeps these ids). Diagnostics are `MSA_*`. Assembly's reason codes are namespaced `MSA.<CODE>` under the kernel's `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)`. Every new number carries `[PLACEHOLDER]` and a registry-candidate line (see *Names this GDD introduces*, end of this section). Neighbour rules are cited by rule id (`LS-15`, `LY-16`, `BDY-24`, `IA-14`), never by line number, because sibling GDDs are still being edited. "Advisor R<n>" names an orchestrator ruling that decided the point; "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" names a reconciliation made while authoring. Each rule gives **Rule**, **Criterion** (AC ids), **Pillar**, an *Alternative considered* line where a choice was made, and *Decides*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* One tag is added: `[VS-B]` marks a co-op rule, target or criterion (it needs a second seat, a MIRROR client or a crewmate's presence) and is excluded from the MVP gate; the one-weld-versus-three-verbs contingency is stated once, in the Overview. No fault rule relies on an exception being thrown or caught: GDScript has none (MSA-31).
134	
135	#### A. Shape of the system
136	
137	**MSA-1 — Five commands, three families.** *Rule:* Assembly registers exactly five command types (table T1). **Family W (weld):** `begin_weld` (PLAYER, CHANNEL) and `weld` (SYSTEM, the atomic completion). **Family C (seam cut):** `begin_seam_cut` (PLAYER, CHANNEL) and `seam_cut` (SYSTEM, the atomic completion). **Family I (install):** `install_module` (PLAYER, TAP). The `begin_*` commands open a channel and mutate no ship state; the completions are the atomic cross-block applies; install is a one-shot atomic apply. No other type is registered. `remove_module` is reserved and unregistered (MSA-28). The name `begin_cut` is Interaction's V8 module salvage and is never used here; `CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` and `SALVAGE_*` are likewise never reused. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-01. *Pillar:* P5, anti-pillar "not a freeform builder" (three pre-shaped verbs). *Decides:* advisor R1, R4, R5, R10, R27.
138	
139	**T1 — Command types** (registry: `assembly_commands`).
140	
141	| Command | Origin | Mode | Payload (primitives only) | Actor binding | Coalesce | `max_age_ticks` | Declared / registered | Reason set |
142	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
143	| `begin_weld` | PLAYER | CHANNEL | `{target_ref}` (a `WELD_SOCKET` subject in `FREE`) | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | `MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION` 120 (kernel, cited) | Interaction declares the row (IA-23); Assembly registers | `weld_ready`, IMMEDIATE half (T2); tool `tool_welder` |
144	| `begin_seam_cut` | PLAYER | CHANNEL | `{target_ref}` (a `WELD_SOCKET` subject in `WELDED`) | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | 120 | declaration row requested of Interaction (ASK I1); Assembly registers | `seam_cut_ready`, IMMEDIATE half; tool `tool_cutter`; `CUT_BLOCKED` |
145	| `weld` | SYSTEM | atomic completion | `{actor, socket_a, socket_b, cause}`, `cause` = `CHANNEL` | explicit `actor` field (SYSTEM origin has no issuer binding) | `NONE` | `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` 12 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (MSA-6) | Assembly | `weld_ready` full; DEFERRED branch resolves to `BLOCKED` |
146	| `seam_cut` | SYSTEM | atomic completion | `{actor, seam_id, cause}`, `cause` in {`CHANNEL`, `CASCADE`} | explicit `actor` field | `NONE` | `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` 12 | Assembly | `can_detach` set, `CUT_BLOCKED` |
147	| `install_module` | PLAYER | TAP | `{hardpoint_ref}` | `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` `body.state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | `NONE` | 120 | declaration row requested of Interaction (ASK I1); Assembly registers | IMMEDIATE set only; DEFERRED branch resolves to `BLOCKED` |
148	
149	All reasons are computed from true state and the kernel never filters them (CR-5). `allowed_origins` of `weld` and `seam_cut` is SYSTEM only (a channel completion or a cascade); tests submit them through a SYSTEM-origin double.
150	
151	**MSA-2 — Assembly owns decisions, not mutations.** *Rule:* Assembly owns the five commands, the weld quality `q`, the channel durations, the offer predicates, the cut-mode derivation, the order of mutator calls inside each apply, `assembly.state`, `assembly.step`, and its reason codes. It owns no geometry (Layout), no seam edges, atmosphere or the formulas `cap_seam`, `hp_seam`, `A_seam_m` (Graph), no pose, velocity or actors (Body), no item vocabulary (Item DB), and no channel clock, abort set, partial-progress ledger or noise (Interaction). Every state change goes through a mutator the owning system publishes (kernel CR-9; H1, H3). Assembly writes exactly one block, its own. It adds no arithmetic of its own to the Graph's seam formulas: it supplies `q` and `L_seam` and cites `LSG D.14` and `LSG D.2` (D.4 below works them at MVP values). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-02 (review: no restated foreign arithmetic or value), AC-MSA-03 (lint: the only block Assembly writes is `assembly.state`; every other write is a published mutator). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* advisor R2; KRN H1, H3.
152	
153	**MSA-3 — Weld and seam cut are two-phase: begin, accrue, handoff, completion.** *Rule:*
154	
155	1. **Begin (P2 of tick `Tb`, PLAYER).** `begin_weld {target_ref}` or `begin_seam_cut {target_ref}`. `validate` runs the IMMEDIATE half of the predicate only (MSA-7, MSA-8). `apply` calls Interaction's proposed Class B `open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks)` and the Controller's `set_channel_ref(actor, ASSEMBLY, channel_id, face_octant)` (published, PC-1 b; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*), where `face_octant = octant_of(anchor_o(target_ref) − foot)` is computed in this apply (Controller D.8: the octant whose D.3 `UNIT` vector maximises the integer dot product, ties to the smaller index; `NONE` only for a zero vector), `anchor_o` being the interaction anchor of the `target_ref` subject (the `WELD_SOCKET` subject for `begin_weld`, the seam subject for `begin_seam_cut`, the same anchor Interaction's `in_reach` uses) and `foot` the actor's `pos_curr`, both in the actor's body frame; the Controller stores it as `channel_face` and locks facing to it for the channel *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, CONFLICT)*; the apply mutates no ship state. Coalesce `NONE`.
156	2. **Accrue (P3, Interaction).** `interaction.step` runs the clock, the shared abort set, the lit recheck, the partial-progress ledger and the noise exactly as for its own verbs (MSA-30). Per IA-14, elapsed `e = T - Tb` and accrual happens at `e = 1..D`, so a fresh channel is DONE on the P3 of tick `Tb + D` (a channel resumed from the ledger is DONE `resume_offset` ticks sooner; the arithmetic below is for a fresh one).
157	3. **Handoff (P3 of tick `Tb + D`, `assembly.step`, ordered after `interaction.step`).** It reads the DONE handoff Interaction exposes in `channel_view` and re-runs the IMMEDIATE predicate. On a fail it writes `last_result = REJECTED(reason)` and submits nothing (the channel's cost is spent; the cause is world-visible). On a pass it writes `pending {kind, target_ref, submit_T}` and submits the SYSTEM-origin completion `weld {actor, socket_a, socket_b, cause CHANNEL}` or `seam_cut {actor, seam_id, cause CHANNEL}`.
158	4. **Completion (P2 of tick `Tb + D + 1`).** Authority, then `validate` proves everything by pure reads (MSA-7, MSA-14, MSA-20), then `apply` is total.

170	*Why that makes the two outcomes exclusive by construction.* A hook-submitted command is stamped `queued_tick = submit_T`. So the command can apply only while `k <= PENDING_TTL_TICKS`; at `k = PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1` P2 rejects it `STALE` and the P3 of that same tick (after P2) is the first tick on which `T - submit_T > PENDING_TTL_TICKS` and `assembly.step` may write `NOT_TAKEN`. No late `Applied` can follow a `NOT_TAKEN`, and no `NOT_TAKEN` precedes an apply. Constraint (formula D.11): `PENDING_TTL_TICKS >= ceil(QUEUE_CAPACITY / MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK)` = 8, which is the kernel's own never-stale invariant (`KRN D.7`: `max_age_ticks(any type) >= 8`), so a local command is never spuriously stale from queue depth; default 12, range 8-119 `[PLACEHOLDER]`. **One guarantee, the BUSY gate** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `pending.kind != NONE` is a `BUSY` term at site 1 only (MSA-7), so a `begin_*` pressed while a completion is unresolved is refused at the prompt rather than queued behind it; this, not a duration floor, is what makes it impossible for a new handoff to meet an unresolved `pending` (a resumed channel can be as short as 6 ticks, D.7, so a floor on channel length proves nothing). The range tops out at 119 because of clause 2 (`MAX_AGE_TICKS_ACTION` 120 minus 1). A rejection at admission (`QUEUE_FULL`) or in P2 leaves `pending` set, so the same TTL covers it; the cue arrives `PENDING_TTL_TICKS + 1` = 13 ticks (about 0.22 s) after submission, which is acceptable for a neutral cue. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: in that window the pending target may already be `WELDED` (a rival completion applied first, E-7, AC-MSA-59) or the seam already `CUT`. 216	#### C. Weld
217	
218	**MSA-11 — Host and mate selection: the home-ship side goes first.** *Rule:* the Graph's section `kind` (LS-17: HOME or DERELICT) decides the order. `socket_a` is the socket whose section has `kind` HOME; the other is `socket_b`. The seat may stand on either side and may focus either socket; Assembly derives the ordered pair, so the surviving body is always the home-ship's and the absorbed derelict body is re-based (this answers Layout's LY-16 host-rule clarification and Open Question 21: confirmed). The **mate** is the unique `FREE` socket `b` for which `can_attach(a, b)` passes **and** `docked(a, b, frame_shift_px)` holds. Two non-home bodies `[VS]` tie-break on the lower `body_id`; several mates `[VS]` tie-break on the lowest `(socket_key_a, socket_key_b)` (formula D.3). MVP has exactly one pair: `sock_airlock_e` (home-ship, facing E) and `sock_b_w` (derelict B, facing W), `class_id` 1 (`SOCKET_CLASS` = DOCK_STD), `width_tiles` 2, lanes POWER lane 0 and O₂ lane 0, no COOLANT lane, one hatch each, weld offset `(696, 384)`. Assembly repeats the lane set and the offset as Derelict Authoring's must-repeat asks (DA-10). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-15. *Pillar:* P5 (the home-ship body survives). *Decides:* advisor R14; LY-16.
219	
220	**MSA-12 — The player weld is offered only once the pair is docked.** *Rule:* `weld_offer(seat, socket)` is a pure read published by Assembly (formula D.2) and is the `eligible` predicate of Interaction's `begin_weld` declaration row: it is true iff the welder is the equipped tool, the seat is `lit` and `in_reach` of the socket, the socket is `FREE`, a unique mate passes `can_attach`, and `docked(a, b, frame_shift_px)` holds. No prompt exists unless the offer holds. `NOT_DOCKED` exists only as a backstop (T2). Web Map & Transit establishes `docked` (WM-21 `berth`; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: no longer provisional*); Body tests it; Assembly gates the *offer*, as BDY-27 asks ("the offer, not Body's `validate`, is gated"), so the player never sees "the ship jerking". Four consequences. (1) `weld_offer` reads only tool, light, reach, Layout socket state and Body `docked`; it never calls `can_join_static` or the full `can_join`, never reads a node or edge accessor and never reads `surge[]`, and it is a hot-path read (cached static half, O(1) `docked`; its per-call budget is `MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US`, a placeholder in T9 whose value the spike sets). (2) `eligible` currently has one member, `actor_sane_gate` (IA-2), so adding `weld_offer` is an ASK to Interaction; the dependency runs Interaction -> Assembly read view while Assembly calls Interaction's mutators, so it is an injected read-view lookup, not a code import -> ADR candidate. (3) The channel lasts 360 ticks, so Transit could separate a pair during it: the mitigation order is (i) ASK to Transit — do not break `docked` for a pair while an ASSEMBLY weld channel is open on it (readable from `channel_view`) *(answered: WM-22 holds `docked` and makes `pod_hop`, `berth` and `unberth` `BUSY` while an ASSEMBLY channel is open; Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; (ii) the handoff pre-check re-tests `docked` (T2a), which closes all but one tick. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: Body's open request is accepted and the former fallback (iii) is deleted: the Pipeline's `BODY_TRANSFER` camera cut hides camera motion, not the exterior hull jump (BDY-27), so the offer never drops the `docked` term; `docked` is a hard term of the offer, closed by (i) and (ii).)* *(orchestrator ruling: the technical-director's option B, re-checking `docked` in the completion `validate`, is rejected because Body's locked text says weld legality takes no pose input; the handoff re-check is not a kernel `validate`, so it does not contradict it.)* (4) The visual cursor is Layout-supplied data drawn in world space (UI Requirements). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-16 (auto: offer false when not docked, no prompt), AC-MSA-17 (lint + spike: `weld_offer` source calls no `can_join*` or node accessor and meets its budget). *Pillar:* P1. *Alternative considered:* not gating and relying on the camera cut — kept as the named fallback only. *Decides:* advisor R17; BDY-27; TD-8, TD-16.
221	
222	**MSA-13 — `q` is a data constant: never an input, never displayed.** *Rule:* `q = WELD_Q_DEFAULT` 850 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, loaded from the data file, range **`Q_MIN`(`LEAK_HP`) to 990, stated once in D.1** (400 to 990 at the default `LEAK_HP` 4000) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: every other mention of the range in this GDD cites D.1 instead of restating it)*, default 850 *(refines advisor R11, which ruled 400-1000: LSG D.2's floor form gives `A_seam_m` 0 from birth only at `q` of 993 or more, and 0 once `leak_bp` is low enough, and the Graph's own `SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP` row calls "welds never weep" an R9 violation, so q 1000 would delete the weld's P1 tell)*. There is no player input, no modifier slot and no `Σ q_mods` term anywhere in the rules; the Vertical Slice options (a hold-longer trade, a weld-rod part) appear in Open Questions only, because a modifier slot in the rules invites progression creep. `q` goes into the plan handed to `weld_join` and the Graph stores it on the SeamRecord. `q` is never shown in any prompt, preview, tooltip or player-visible debug HUD; the Debug Overlay reads the true value. Its consequences are physical and come from the Graph, cited and never restated as Assembly's: `cap_seam` is 925 permille of the lesser port at q 850, `hp_seam` is 8500 (above `HP_OK` 7000), `leak_bp` starts at `SEAM_LEAK_INITIAL_BP` 10000 unscaled, and the D.2 seam area `A_seam_m` gives the weep (`LSG D.14`, `LSG D.2`; worked in D.4). **Named cliffs for the knob.** Below 400, `hp_seam = q * 10` falls below `LEAK_HP` 4000 and every MVP weld would start leaking at birth, which breaks P2 fairness (a leak with no prior tell); data outside the range is clamped at **both** ends, to `Q_MIN` (400 at the default `LEAK_HP`) or to 990, and logged `MSA_Q_CLAMPED`. **The upper cliff is q of 993 or more** (q = 1000 is the limiting case, LSG D.2 Output Range): `A_seam_m` is 0 from birth, the seam has no weep, and the weld's own P1 tell vanishes; at q 990 (`Q_MAX`) the fresh seam still weeps, at 2 milli flow units, for about 6.3 minutes (worked in D.1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **The lower cliff is q < 400**, named above. Default 850 keeps the Graph's q-dependent paths exercised only at one value in play; the Graph side tests q 400 and 1000. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-18 (lint: clamp and diagnostic), AC-MSA-19 (lint: `q` reaches no player-visible string or UI path), AC-MSA-20 (review: no modifier term). *Pillar:* P1, anti-progression. *Alternative considered:* `q` from hold time, a consumed weld rod or tool condition — rejected for MVP (channel length would become player-variable, no such Item DB def exists, tools have no durability). *Decides:* advisor R11; `LSG D.14`.
223	
224	**MSA-14 — The weld `apply` runs in one fixed order; every call has a named proof.** *Rule:* after the completion's `validate` passes and the A0 deferred check is clear, `apply` runs in this order (table T3): Graph M2 `weld_join(plan)` -> Layout LM2 `attach_section(socket_a, socket_b, seam_id, welded_at_T)` -> Body BM3 `rebase_on_attach(surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, frame_shift_px)` -> Interaction `sync_section(section_a)` and `sync_section(section_b)` -> `assembly.state` (clear `pending`, write `last_result = DONE`). The order Graph -> Layout -> Body is Body's (BDY-21): BM3 or BM4 before its Layout mutator is `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, a defect. Assembly allocates no id; the `seam_id` that LM2 needs is returned by M2 *(answered 2026-10-27: Graph LS-15, `weld_join` returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`; Layout Open Question 4 closed; Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and without that return the chain cannot be written (fallback: Assembly allocates, which advisor R6 rejects on H3 grounds). The apply is infallible *by proof*, not by hope: each call's precondition is a pure read already run in `validate`, and a call with no proving read is a FAULTED path and a design defect (TD-1). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **fault detection is explicit, because GDScript has no throw and no catch.** A runtime error ends the function with a default return and the caller carries on; `assert()` is compiled out of a release export. "Infallible by proof" therefore needs a detector that does not depend on either. The contract (MSA-31): every Class A mutator Assembly calls (M2, LM2, BM3 for a weld; M3, LM3, BM4 for a cut; M5 for an install) returns a status, `OK` or a `FAULT_CODE` naming the violated precondition; Assembly's `apply` checks the status after **every** call, and on the first non-`OK` it calls `ctx.fault(code, detail)` (kernel CR-19(a), ASK K2 answered *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) and returns `ctx.complete()` at once, making no further mutator call. A mutator that returns `OK` but leaves a cross-block disagreement is caught by the release postconditions of MSA-32 (INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5 and INV-7 after each weld or cut) and by the always-on integer comparisons `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT` (A3 against A4) and `MSA_VERDICT_DRIFT` (A0 against V4), which are promoted from debug assertions to release-fatal faults.)* One P5 notification batch results, with the Graph's keys `T`, `S/<seam_id>`, `SEC/<a>`, `SEC/<b>` (and nothing else from the Graph) plus Layout's `BODY/` and `SEC/` keys for moved sections and Body's keys. Weld `apply` is integer arithmetic only: no RNG, no wall-clock (H9). The Graph's keyed draws (`rng_derive(world_seed, "graph.fail", (step_no << 20) | subject_id)`) are unchanged by a weld or a cut because a weld only appends ids and never renumbers (LS-9, LS-15), so replay identity across a weld needs no Assembly term. Budget: M2 alone <= 0.2 ms Release (locked, Graph); the whole weld `apply` is a placeholder budget measured in the spike (Tuning Knobs). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-21 (auto: recorded call trace equals the T3 order; a BM call before its Layout call raises `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`), AC-MSA-22 (auto: exact P5 batch keys), AC-MSA-23 (spike: budget), AC-MSA-24 (auto: a table-driven test enumerates T3 and asserts every apply call has a proof entry), AC-MSA-142 and AC-MSA-143 (auto: a mutator returning a `FAULT_CODE`, and a half-applied A3, each fault the kernel in a release-configured build) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Pillar:* P1 (the world is never half-welded). *Decides:* advisor R6, R10; KRN CR-9; BDY-21.

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`

- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`

> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

526	**Tick-order facts the rows above depend on.** Within one tick, P2 (commands: the `begin_*` applies, the completions, install) precedes P3 (hooks). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* The Graph hooks run on separate ticks (power at `T mod 6 = 0`, atmo at 2, failure at 4, Graph LS-8); on any tick the P3 order is the resolved order, in which whichever Graph hook is due runs before `emitter.place` -> `interaction.step` -> `assembly.step` (IA-14: through the `emitter.place` chain). The weld applies in P2, so the first Graph hook that runs after it (power, atmo or failure, whichever is due next) refreshes the topology (Graph phase 1 refresh at the head of any hook) and sees the bumped `topology_version` and the new seam, so no half-state is observable. A completion submitted in `assembly.step` in P3 of `T` is dispatched in P2 of `T+1`. Body's mutators run after Layout's, which run after the Graph's, inside one `WriteScope`.

286	**MSA-23 — A cut's mode must be predictable from the world alone.** *Rule:* at any moment between "prompt offered" and "channel complete", a player who has looked at the seam within the last `CUT_WITNESS_LOOKBACK_S` 60 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (a manual-AC parameter for AC-MSA-39, not a sim knob, and unrelated to `OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS`) can tell from the world alone whether the cut will be SEALED or RAGGED. If a fresh weld could emit `SEAL_STRAIN` on a closed hatch with a latent gradient, the "quiet seam" witness would be false, which is why the first-connect beat needs a small or deliberate gradient (a verify handed to the Graph and Derelict Authoring owners). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, three corrections.)* **(1) "Quiet" is scoped.** The Graph's LS-15 says an as-welded seam "is not quiet": it weeps (a HISS at the seam) from its first run until wear-in ends (about 16.7 minutes). The seam weep's hiss is anchored on the bead and loops, an open seam valve's hiss is anchored on the lane; Failure & Trail must keep the two distinguishable by anchor (ASK FT2, `[UNV]`, a playtest item of AC-MSA-39). **(2) Starting gradient is a content requirement, not a verify.** The first connect (Beat 2) must have something to read, so Derelict Authoring must author derelict B's starting state so that at least one of `SEAL_STRAIN` (a pressure difference over `WELD_DP_WARN`) or rim frost (a temperature difference over `HATCH_DT_FROST_MC`) fires on the closed seam hatch on the first Graph step after the weld (ASK D3; visually at once, its creak sounds after the 1 s quiet window of Beat 1 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*); AC-MSA-140 is the fixture check. This does not make the seam lie: it is B's true state. **(3) MSA-23b, "feel the seam",** is added below as the hand-on-the-seam witness. **(4) What is BLOCKING and what is not.** AC-MSA-126 (the TRUTH fallback) stays gating. The BLOCKING label is removed from AC-MSA-39 and AC-MSA-93: with FT1 answered and the fallback in force, they depend on playtest evidence and on the Graph's G8 answer, not on a missing mechanism. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-39 (manual: pooled, at least 17 of 20 judgements correct across 5 first-time players and 4 scenarios, no ragged cut reported as "random"; see Validation targets for the scoring rule). *Pillar:* P1, P2. *Decides:* game-designer G9.

288	**MSA-23b — Feel the seam: a QUIET consequence-channel read at the seam. `[PROVISIONAL — ASK IW1]`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; creative-director position, game-designer option (a))*. *Rule:* the Inspect View owner (In-World Instruments & Inspect View, Designed) defines a QUIET, no-tool, no-noise `inspect` read on the seam's hatch frame: while the seat holds `inspect` within `REACH_PX` of a `WELDED` seam's frame for the owner's hold time, the presenter shows the **true positions** the cut mode reads (D.6): the hatch leaf open or shut, each seam sub-edge valve open or shut, the seam breaker open or closed, as the existing TRUTH wheel and lever frames, enlarged and held in the card grammar the owner already has. It delivers the Player Fantasy promise "put my hand on the seam" (L44, L76). It is not a seam-health readout. *If IW1 is declined:* L44 and L76 are rewritten to the witnesses that exist (hiss, creak, frost, the true seam-lane sprites) and the fallback of MSA-23 stays in force permanently. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-145 (auto, with an Inspect View double) and AC-MSA-126 (unchanged, still gating). *Pillar:* P1, P4.

292	**MSA-25 — Sockets are terminal.** *Rule:* a socket goes `FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED` (SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (RAGGED cut) and **never back to `FREE`** in MVP (LY-13). Weld, then cut, then a second weld attempt on the same socket yields `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` in the world with no prompt; the playtest gate must not require a second weld. Illegal transitions: `FREE -> CAPPED`, `WELDED -> FREE`, `CAPPED -> WELDED`, any state to `FREE`. There is no `install_cap_plate` and no `set_socket_state` mutator (LY-27): a socket's state changes only inside LM2 and LM3, atomic with the Graph's weld and cut. The socket economy (one home socket, terminal scars, net cycle minus one) is **not solved here** and is recorded `[VS]` with Layout's three options (a re-cut verb that reopens a `CAPPED` socket keeping history; more home sockets; derelicts that bring three or more sockets) and the lint `SOCKET_ECONOMY_LOW`. **It is an explicit Vertical Slice GATE criterion, not an open question (CD-GDD-ALIGN):** MVP can play the core P5 loop (salvage integrates into the body that survives; deeper is richer) exactly once, which is acceptable for MVP only; the Vertical Slice may not close, and `/gate-check` may not pass it, until one option is chosen, authored and played through `VS_WELD_CYCLES_MIN` `[PLACEHOLDER]` 3 consecutive weld cycles with `SOCKET_ECONOMY_LOW` silent (AC-MSA-125, Open Question 7), so that "net cycle minus one" cannot ship past the Vertical Slice and leave the assembly fantasy unrepeatable. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-41 (auto: weld, cut, second weld returns `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, no prompt). *Pillar:* P5. *Decides:* advisor R20, R22; LY-13.

296	**MSA-26 — Install is Assembly's own TAP, with a carve-out to carrying.** *Rule:* `install_module {hardpoint_ref}` (PLAYER, TAP). The prompt exists iff the seat carries an instance whose def is in `compatible_defs(h)` for the focused HARDPOINT subject; that is static Item DB data, so it is IMMEDIATE, and an incompatible install is simply never offered (Item DB: "refused with `PORT_INCOMPAT`, never offered"). IMMEDIATE `validate`: kernel authority, carrying, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `NOT_LIT`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `NOT_ELIGIBLE`, not staggered or downed, and a `PORT_INCOMPAT` backstop. **CONFLICT against two locked GDDs (C1, ANSWERED: PC-8 and IA-28 now carry the carve-out, AC-IA-78; Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review):** the Controller's PC-8 and Interaction's IA-28 both rejected "every `interact` mode except `drop`" while carrying as `BUSY`. Carve-out sentence for the Controller owner (PC-8) and the Interaction owner (IA-28): *"while carrying, `interact` on a HARDPOINT subject whose `compatible_defs(h)` lists the carried instance's def is admitted, alongside `drop`."* ASK to Interaction (ASK I1): a declaration row, object class HARDPOINT, `tool_required` NONE, a carry precondition, owner Assembly, `noise_class` QUIET. The `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut` CHANNELS stay inadmissible while carrying (PC-7; a torch needs two hands). *Named fallback if the Controller owner refuses:* drop first, then install from LOOSE_WORLD with bare hands, which amends the Item DB's instance row 8 instead (source state LOOSE_WORLD). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-42 (auto: prompt iff the carried def is compatible), AC-MSA-43 (auto: every other `interact` mode is still `BUSY` while carrying). *Pillar:* P5, anti-pillar. *Alternative considered:* (a) install as a `drop` onto a hardpoint — rejected: silently overloads Interaction's `drop` and a mis-drop installs; (c) drop-then-install — rejected as primary: the module lies loose between steps and the trophy is on the floor before the payoff. *Decides:* advisor R1.
297	
298	**MSA-27 — Install `apply`: check first, then the chain (table T5).** *Rule:* `apply` first calls the pure Graph `check_install_module` (Item DB spelling). On a fail it writes `last_result = BLOCKED(SLOT_OCCUPIED)` (Assembly's outcome name for the Graph's "slot not ABSENT or SALVAGED" failure; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* the Graph's M5 row now names that reason `SLOT_OCCUPIED` itself, so the mapping is one to one and ASK G9 is closed) (or `BLOCKED(PORT_INCOMPAT)` as a backstop), changes nothing else and the instance stays carried (IA-24's TAP-outcome precedent). On a pass, in order: Graph M5 `install_module(slot_node_id, def_id, hp_start := condition_bp, hp_cap := cap_bp, patched_at_step)` -> Suit `release_carried(player_id)` (SE-13; "Suit never self-releases") -> Controller `clear_carry_ref(actor)` *(published by the Controller, PC-1 b and PC-8; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*)* -> Interaction `sync_section(section_id)` -> `last_result = DONE`. The instance dissolves (Item DB row 8: CARRIED -> INSTALLED). A new store's stock is 0. Cap and decay-clock carry-through follows Item DB IDB-18. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **answered by the Graph; the earlier "provisional, AC blocked" text is withdrawn.** M5 now takes `hp_cap` (default `HP_FULL`) and `patched_at_step` (default 0): "a patched module reinstalls capped and keeps its absolute `patched_at_step` decay clock; a store installs empty" (Graph M5 row, consistency pass 2026-10-27). The install apply therefore passes `hp_start := condition_bp`, `hp_cap := cap_bp` and `patched_at_step := patched_at_step` from the carried instance's fields (Item DB instance rows `condition_bp`, `cap_bp`, `patched_at_step`) in the same single M5 call, so no second mutator call and no new FAULTED row are added. ASK G5 is closed for the install; AC-MSA-44 asserts the carry-through; the hull-plate and seam-repair halves of IDB Open Questions 11 and 12 stay open and are not Assembly's.)* No Emitter call (no `mod_lamp` install exists in MVP; an ASK if one is added). There is no sim seating timer: the seating cue and the install clunk are presentation, Assembly's by the Item DB. A running machine begins its loop only if the Graph runs it. The `BLOCKED` result is a free probe of slot occupancy in one direction (a false-system-state hallucination could show a slot empty), while the opposite direction costs an irreversible install; a short per-seat lockout after `BLOCKED` is proposed by the game-designer but would add state to `assembly.state`, so it is not adopted here (Open Questions). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-44 (auto: chain order), AC-MSA-45 (auto: `BLOCKED` leaves the instance carried and every block unchanged but `assembly.state`). *Pillar:* P5, P4 (state read admitted, MSA-9). *Decides:* advisor R18; IA-24; TD ledger 2.3.

(The cut never takes the weld's sputter: the cut's bead is already laid, and the cut is the verb that fails to *separate* it.) The reason code is in the result event for DIAGNOSTIC and replay only. A distinct cue per reason would be the reason text P4 forbids; the cost is that the player cannot tell `PORT_ABSENT` from `NOT_TAKEN` by the cue alone, which is acceptable because both are rare in MVP and the world answers within one walk. Every non-DONE outcome has a world witness reachable within about 60 s: `PORT_ABSENT` leaves the lane node's hardpoint footprint visible as an empty bay (Layout keeps a MACHINE footprint after salvage, LY-20); `SLOT_OCCUPIED` shows the occupying module at the bay; `NOT_TAKEN` means a world fact changed during the channel.
