Durations: `WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS` 360 (6 s, range 240-480) and `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240 (4 s, range 240-480), both `[PLACEHOLDER]` feel values from the Controller's Open Question 7, both multiples of `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 (the IA I-2 lint: 60 and 40 blocks), both in the LONG bar class (`BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS` 240, so the floor is 240, not lower). The ceiling 480 is set by analogy with IA I-9 (which bounds Interaction's own LONG bar at twice `BAR_LONG_FROM_TICKS`), cited as an analogy, not a lock on Assembly. `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` and Interaction's `SALVAGE_CHANNEL_TICKS` happen to share 240 at MVP but are distinct names (the Controller's "cut 240" is ambiguous between them). The cut is deliberately faster than the weld: both verbs are terminal on their socket, so neither is a repeatable exploit, and the cut is a prepared amputation paid for by a `LOUD` completion and a possible breach *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "the P5 escape verb" is deleted. The cut is not an escape verb: a panic cut is RAGGED and breaches the home side, and the Player Fantasy states three prepared reasons to cut)*; revisit if players use it as a free panic button, which would show as RAGGED cuts under attack in the playtest log, not as a reason to make the cut slower. Duration never depends on any state (IA-11c); movement cancels (PC-7: "I can leave now"). `abort_channel(actor)` (IA-35's proposed Assembly mutator) is **refused**: `cancel_channel` already ends an ASSEMBLY-owned record held in `interaction.state`, so Assembly publishes no cancel. Asks to Interaction (all under ASK I1; numbering as in T15): I1(i) a third Class B mutator `open_channel(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks)` called by the two `begin_*` applies (IA-1 says Interaction publishes "exactly two" Class B mutators, so this is a refresh); I1(ii) `channel_view` exposes, for the tick on which it happens, a DONE handoff `(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref)` for records with `owner_system` other than INTERACTION, and at that DONE Interaction applies nothing itself except to clear `channel_ref` through the Controller mutator (IA-14 row 9) and delete any ledger entry; I1(iii) `begin_weld` and `begin_seam_cut` join IA-16's list of non-incremental channels; I1(viii), answered (IA-14 row 6): for ASSEMBLY-owned records the NOT_ELIGIBLE abort re-tests the owner's `eligible` predicate at `LIT_RECHECK_TICKS`, so a lost `docked` aborts the channel *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-49 (lint: both durations multiples of 6 within 240-480), AC-MSA-50 (auto: abort resumes from the ledger within `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` and not after). *Pillar:* P3, P2. *Decides:* advisor R2, R13; IA-14, IA-15, IA-16, IA-35, PC-7. CONFLICTS C3, C4.

**MSA-31 — Atomicity, the failure model and what a defect costs.** *Rule:* each completion `apply` and the install `apply` is atomic against every other command, hook and snapshot (CR-9), followed by one P5 notification batch per block (CR-10). Dirty keys are marked explicitly in every mutator (Godot 4.7 packed-array element writes call no setter). `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256 is not approached if `sync_section` marks only changed subjects (formula D.12). The failure model is **validate-then-apply, no rollback**: `validate` proves everything through read-only queries, `apply` is infallible by contract, and a failure inside `apply` is a defect that moves the kernel `RUNNING -> FAULTED`: the faulting command is `Faulted(code)` and every other pending command is `Dropped(FAULTED)` (kernel CR-5, CR-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save, and in a development build halts with diagnostics. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **how the defect is detected.** The kernel's CR-9 edge case says the kernel "aborts the current `apply` at the assertion" and the earlier text of this rule, E-35, S6 and AC-MSA-51 assumed an `apply` can throw and a batch loop can catch it. GDScript has no throw, try or catch: a runtime error ends the function with a default return and the caller carries on, and `assert()` does not exist in a release export. So detection is **explicit**: (1) every cross-block mutator Assembly calls returns a status, `OK` or a `FAULT_CODE`; (2) the `apply` checks the status after every call and, on the first non-`OK`, calls `ctx.fault(code, detail)` (kernel CR-19(a); the published mutators report on the shared `WriteScope` with `scope.fault` and return their status) and returns `ctx.complete()` without a further mutator call *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (3) the release build runs the postconditions of MSA-14 and MSA-32 after each weld or cut (statuses, `MSA_SHIFT_DRIFT`, `MSA_VERDICT_DRIFT`, INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-7), so a half-applied A3 (Layout written, Body not) is caught by A4's status or, failing that, by INV-4 and INV-5 instead of surviving; (4) the "defect" tested in S6 and AC-MSA-51 is "a mutator returns a `FAULT_CODE` or violates a postcondition", never "throws". The kernel has made this correction (CR-19, CONFLICT C14 closed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R3)* **Callable contract:** every kernel-invoked Assembly callable (`validate` of the five command types, `apply`, `assembly.step`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`) receives the kernel's `ctx`, reports through it (`ctx.ok()` or `ctx.reject(reason)` in `validate`, `ctx.put(payload)` in `snapshot`, `ctx.fault(code, detail)` on a defect) and has `return ctx.complete()` as its only return statement; none is declared `-> void`, and a published mutator takes the shared `WriteScope`, reports with `scope.fault` and returns a status that the `apply` propagates. Verified against the engine reference: it has no scripting module, so whether Godot 4.7.2 offers a custom `Logger` that sees script errors is `[UNV]` and is not relied upon.)* The only exits are an explicit user `request_restore` or shutdown. **This is not Save/Load's MVP death rule** (SL-7, restart from the last autosave), which is a separate mechanism with the same loading path; the two must not be conflated. The price of "no rollback", stated plainly: the loss window for an Assembly defect (`fault_loss_ticks`, D.16) is up to 18000 ticks (5 minutes of play, `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` 10800 + `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200) at the ceiling, 10800 at the maximum when no soft gate defers the interval save, and about 5400 on average (half the interval, because a defect lands uniformly inside it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "10800 typical" was a maximum, not a typical value; D.16)*, after the player chooses to load. These figures are the bound without an event save, which a defect inside an apply still meets, because the apply's own event save comes after it; weld and cut completions are autosave *events* in the MVP (user ruling D17, MSA-33), which shorten the window for any later defect *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. No pre-weld checkpoint is added: autosave is soft-gated while `CHANNELLING` (SL-5) and a checkpoint would be a second transaction. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-51 (auto, fault injection: a stub mutator that returns a `FAULT_CODE` or violates a postcondition at A3 and A4, and a forced verifier failure, each leave the kernel FAULTED with the faulting command `Faulted(code)`, every other pending command `Dropped(FAULTED)`, the existing save untouched, and `request_restore` returning a state-hash-equal world; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "throws" removed*), AC-MSA-142, AC-MSA-143, AC-MSA-148. *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* KRN CR-9, CR-10, CR-17, CR-18; advisor R25.

**MSA-32 — A read-only cross-block integrity verifier is the compensating control for "no rollback".** *Rule:* the Graph protects itself (LS-24), Layout and Body each assert their own tables, but nobody owns a check that the three agree, and the three-owner split is exactly what makes each owner's check blind to the others' disagreement. Assembly therefore owns a **read-only verifier** of the **cross-owner** invariants in T7: INV-1 to INV-7 and INV-10, eight in all. Conservation and fresh-seam disconnection (T7's former INV-8 and INV-9) are Graph-internal invariants the Graph already asserts itself (LS-24), so the verifier does not re-own them; they appear as AC cross-checks that cite LS-24 (AC-MSA-25 for the fresh seam, AC-MSA-67 for conservation). It reads only `SIM` views of Layout, Graph, Body and Interaction (never a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, CR-12), changes nothing, and reports violation ids. Run policy: in `assembly.state`'s `post_restore` (which runs the verifier and clears nothing, the stored `pending` being NONE, MSA-4 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and runs after `layout.state`, `graph.state`, `interaction.state` and `body.state` because of `restore_after`) all eight, **hard** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: except INV-6's `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` half, which is warn-only, MSA-41, because a surplus live body degrades lighting and corrupts nothing)*: a violation fails the restore: LOADING -> FAULTED naming `assembly.state` and the INV id (kernel edge case on `post_restore` failure; whole-block replace means the pre-restore state is not intact); the save file is not modified and the player may choose another restore; never silently continued; after every Assembly apply in debug and CI builds, all eight, as an assertion; in release builds after each weld or cut apply, INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5 and INV-7 only (O(seams + bodies + actors): at most 48 seams given `MAX_SECTIONS` 24 and `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` 4, at most `MAX_BODIES` 8 bodies and `MAX_ACTORS` 8 actors) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: INV-4 and INV-5 join the release subset, because a half-applied A3, Layout written and Body not, breaks exactly those two and the earlier subset of INV-1, INV-2 and INV-7 could not see it; the cost stays inside the `verifier_release` allocation of D.15 and is re-measured by S1)*, a violation moving the kernel to FAULTED naming the invariant id (through `ctx.fault` of MSA-31, kernel CR-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, which is strictly better than playing on in a corrupt state. -> ADR candidate: where cross-block invariants live (Assembly or a kernel integrity service). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-52 (auto: each INV fixture violation reports exactly its id), AC-MSA-53 (auto: a save with an ACTIVE `welds[]` row and no Graph SeamRecord fails restore: the kernel is FAULTED with the block id and the INV id in the diagnostic, no tick runs, and the save file bytes are unchanged). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* TD-14.

**MSA-33 — The autosave event is a derived read.** *Rule:* Assembly publishes the pure read `last_shape_change_T()` (formula D.9): the maximum over Layout's `welds[]` of `welded_at_T` and `cut_at_T`, or NONE. Save/Load polls it at tick boundaries (SL-13); Layout's `S/<seam_id>` key in the P5 batch is the notification. The event names are fixed as `ASSEMBLY_WELD` (the maximum is a `welded_at_T`) and `ASSEMBLY_CUT` (the maximum is a `cut_at_T`), answering Save/Load Open Question 24 for Assembly *(fixed 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*; enabling them is Save/Load's, and **the MVP ships both events enabled** (user ruling D17: the weld, cut and module-cut event autosaves are confirmed) alongside the interval, QUIT and initial saves *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The 64-bit `T` values never travel as JSON numbers (SL-2). **Assembly never calls Save/Load.** **No Graph gate covers a RAGGED cut:** SL-5 soft row (a) counts only `ENDOGENOUS` NODE/EDGE/SEAM descriptors, and a RAGGED cut's hull stubs are `EXOGENOUS` and player-caused (LS-16, "no gate"), so, without the withhold below, an autosave **would land during a self-inflicted RAGGED decompression**; the hard DOWNED/DEAD gate (SL-5) still applies. (This corrects advisor R19, which assumed the gate.) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier "This is accepted" sentences and the optional ASK S1(b) are deleted; the withhold below is the rule.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the earlier acceptance of a save mid-breach is withdrawn for the event save.** MVP death means "restart from the last autosave" (SL-7), so an `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event save that lands mid-breach can reload the player into an unwinnable decompression, which is an unfair failure that the autosave hides. New rule: **a RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event is withheld until the keep-side room has vented (band VACUUM) and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed.** Assembly publishes a second pure read, `ragged_breach_open()`, defined in the amendment below and in D.9 (the keep-side cut room still venting through its hull hole, or a keep-side port still uncapped inside the port ceiling; the data come from the Graph's `seam_view` `cut_sides` and `compartment(cid).band_p`, ASK G10 as amended); Save/Load consumes an `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event only while it is false (ASK S1(b), promoted from optional to requested, and extended to the interval save as a soft-gate row). The alternative of keeping a pre-cut slot is rejected: Save/Load's death rule restores the newest verified generation (SL-8), so an older pre-cut generation is not the one the player gets, and a second slot is a second transaction. A save taken inside the breach window by the interval path may still land after `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200, if the window outlasts the cap, the save is written RISKY (`ASSEMBLY_BREACH`). AC-MSA-130 asserts that a restore from any permitted save is winnable.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2: **the withhold is a function of the breach, not of the event kind.** (a) `ragged_breach_open()` counts only the **keep side** (the sections that keep `body_id` after the cut, `keep_sections`); the leaving orphan never counts and never holds a save (the predicate itself is amended 2026-10-28 below). (b) The withhold is Save/Load F-1's `NOT (ragged_breach_open() AND ASSEMBLY_CUT IN kinds(pending_events))`: keyed on the pending SET, not on the single newest `event_kind`, so a weld latched behind an open-breach cut waits with it (F-1; AC-SL-146 (i)); in the MVP (sockets terminal, LY-13, one weld-then-cut cycle) it gives the same answer for every save as the unconditional form, so D54's "a weld is never withheld" holds for every MVP save. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (c) A ceiling, `RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS` 2400 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, on the **port clause only** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `ports_open` is false from `cut_at_T` plus the ceiling on, so a port nobody caps does not hold the event save forever; the ceiling does not bound the decompression, which ends on the Graph band (VACUUM), not on a timer. (d) `event_due` carries NO settle conjunct: Save/Load owns the function (F-1, registry `autosave_due`) and its form is `event_due = (pending_events != empty) AND elapsed >= AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS AND NOT (ragged_breach_open() AND ASSEMBLY_CUT IN kinds(pending_events))`, `elapsed = T - last_save_T`; Assembly withdraws the third S1 ask (an event-capture settle) and its knob (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1/G3)*. (e) The remaining decompression time of a permitted save is bounded by construction: no autosave of either kind is written inside the window, so none lands while the room is partly vented; a Save & Quit inside it is Save/Load's own RISKY-tagged write (cause `ASSEMBLY_BREACH`).)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions) (X7 / D54): adopted as written. The `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event save of a RAGGED cut is withheld until `ragged_breach_open()` is false, and the open RAGGED window is a soft-gate row for the interval save (bounded by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` 7200, so the D.16 ceiling is unchanged); the `ASSEMBLY_WELD` event and a SEALED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event are never withheld by it. Any bound seat at `vitals_state` CRITICAL or worse is a further soft-gate input of Save/Load's own (X7 (a), Save/Load's rule, not restated here). Formula: D.9.)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **The predicate follows the keep-side room's decompression, not the ports alone (creative-director spot-check of D54; Graph LS-16 gives a RAGGED cut two independent hazards, and the Graph, as owner of the physics, wins, G1).** Definition, used everywhere: `ragged_breach_open() = EXISTS seam s in welds[] with state CUT and boundary RAGGED such that venting(s) OR ports_open(s)`; `venting(s) = EXISTS side IN seam_view(s).cut_sides, side.section_id IN keep_sections(s), EXISTS h IN side.cut_holes: h.a_hole > 0 AND compartment(h.cid).band_p != VACUUM` (the hull hole is still open and the keep-side cut room has not yet fallen below the VACUUM band, P < 100 dkPa, LS-7); `ports_open(s) = (SUM over keep sides of side.uncapped_open_ends) > 0 AND T - cut_at_T < RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS`. (a) The two clauses are the two LS-16 hazards and are independent: `cap_port` (M12, `begin_cap`) closes the fluid-port hiss only and never changes `venting`; the `A_CUT` hull hole (hp 2500) has no subject in the MVP, no verb repairs it, and no verb is added for this (creative-director ruling); the keep-side cut room is lost to vacuum until Vertical Slice content (a plate install on the hardpoint, LS-23 / E 'hull segment reaches hp 0') closes the hole. (b) `venting` has no ceiling: it ends by construction when `band_p` reaches VACUUM (P falls geometrically to a residual of at most `ceil(1/k)` mGU, below 100 dkPa), or earlier when the hole is closed (`a_hole` 0, Vertical Slice) or the section is discarded or jettisoned (a tombstoned compartment reads as not venting). Only the port clause carries `RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS`. (c) A closed hole, a SEALED cut, a cut whose keep-side room is already VACUUM, or a seam with no `cut_sides`: the read is false. (d) Assembly's new Graph reads are `seam_view(seam_id).cut_sides` and `compartment(cid).band_p` (both pure, Graph LS-19; ASK G10). Numbers (Graph D.1 at registry defaults, `G_OPEN` 2, `A_CUT` 24, `GAS_SCALE` 1000, `P0` 1000 dkPa nominal, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, one hole per former opening so `n_holes` 1 for the MVP seam): `k = G_OPEN x A_CUT x n_holes / (V x GAS_SCALE)`; for a keep-side cut room of V = 20 (its other doors closed; the room volume is `[UNV]` until Layout publishes it) `k` = 0.0024 per step, the DECOMP band (P < 400) is reached in `ceil(ln(1000/400)/0.0024)` = 382 steps = 2292 ticks and VACUUM (P < 100) in `ceil(ln(1000/100)/0.0024)` = 960 steps = 5760 ticks (96 s); the simulated value may differ by +-2 steps (floor in D.1). V = 30: `k` = 0.0016, 1440 steps = 8640 ticks. A keep-side room open to a larger connected volume vents more slowly (`k` uses the connected volume), bounded in the worst designed case by `ceil(ln(10) x V_total x 1000 / (2 x 24 x 1000))` steps, e.g. V_total 120: 5757 steps = 34 542 ticks; see E-31 for the listed exposure. The window between the handoff (`pending` set in P3 of `T`) and the apply (P2 of `T+1`, up to `T+8` under queue truncation, or `submit_T + 13` when the completion is rejected or dropped, E-33) is not covered by the channelling gate; a snapshot there stores `pending` as NONE and holds no queued completion, so a restore loses the weld or cut and the player redoes the six seconds (the non-snapshot ticks, MSA-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Closing it is an optional ASK to Save/Load (ASK S1): defer the autosave while `pending_any()` is true (one name: `pending_any()`). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-54 (auto: `last_shape_change_T()` after a weld and a cut; two 32-bit parts or a string at the serialisation boundary). *Pillar:* P5. *Decides:* advisor R19; KRN H3 (one source of truth for history is Layout's `welds[]`).

**MSA-34 — Outcome presentation grammar: one cue, no reason text, the world is the explanation.** *Rule:* REJECTED at begin uses the shared prompt grammar (no prompt, or the standard rejection cue). Every **post-channel non-DONE outcome** (a handoff `REJECTED`, `BLOCKED(PORT_ABSENT)`, `BLOCKED(SLOT_OCCUPIED)`, `NOT_TAKEN`) shares **one** cue per verb family and carries no reason text (registry: `seam_cue_vocabulary`): weld, *the bead sputters and does not hold*; seam cut, *the flame gutters and the seam holds*; install, *the module bumps against the socket and stays in your hands*. (The cut never takes the weld's sputter: the cut's bead is already laid, and the cut is the verb that fails to *separate* it.) The reason code is in the result event for DIAGNOSTIC and replay only. A distinct cue per reason would be the reason text P4 forbids; the cost is that the player cannot tell `PORT_ABSENT` from `NOT_TAKEN` by the cue alone, which is acceptable because both are rare in MVP and the world answers within one walk. Every non-DONE outcome has a world witness reachable within about 60 s: `PORT_ABSENT` leaves the lane node's hardpoint footprint visible as an empty bay (Layout keeps a MACHINE footprint after salvage, LY-20); `SLOT_OCCUPIED` shows the occupying module at the bay; `NOT_TAKEN` means a world fact changed during the channel. A presenter plays an outcome cue only if `last_result` is not empty, `last_result.T` differs from the last value it saw and lies within `OUTCOME_CUE_WINDOW_TICKS` 60 `[PLACEHOLDER]` of the current `T`; a restore never replays a cue (`last_result` is runtime-only and so empty after a restore) and a MIRROR join never replays a stale one. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, three corrections to the dedupe.* (1) `last_result` is runtime-only (MSA-4), so a restore leaves it empty by construction rather than by a clearing step. *(2)* **`last_seen` is initialised on join and on restore** to the value of `last_result.T` the presenter finds at that moment (or to "none" when empty), so a client that joins 30 ticks after a result sees `last_result.T` equal to `last_seen`, not different from it, and plays nothing; the earlier text claimed a join "never plays a stale cue" while `last_seen_T` was unset on a MIRROR join, which would have played it. *(3)* **The dedupe is keyed by `(PlayerId, T)`, not by one scalar `T`,** because results are per seat, and **a presenter plays cues for the local seat only**; a crewmate's result is seen through their channel and the world, never through a cue. D.17 states the formula; AC-MSA-139 tests a join 30 ticks after a result.)* *Criterion:* AC-MSA-55 (review and manual: the cue is identical across the three non-DONE outcomes, none reads as "it worked", the witness is reachable in about 60 s), AC-MSA-56 (auto: `last_result` is consumed once). *Pillar:* P4, P1. *Decides:* advisor R12, R24; TD-13; game-designer G3, G4.

**MSA-35 — The perception boundary.** *Rule:* Assembly reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block (CR-12) and writes no perception state; every Assembly read has no perceived variant; Assembly's presentation never consumes `surge[]` magnitudes, `q`, `leak_bp` or `hp`. A phantom seam or a false "welded" state may exist only in the Perception Filter's corruptible presentation layer; it never reaches `welds[]`, the consequence channel or the bead geometry. Seam geometry, bead, cap plate and socket state are truth channel (an ASK to the Filter repeating LY-34), the seam's own lane valve and breaker sprites are truth channel under the MSA-23 fallback until the zero-gradient witness is confirmed (the same ASK to the Filter, F1), and `CUT_BLOCKED` is a kept truth oracle (MSA-21). No flesh or violet appears anywhere in Assembly's presentation. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-57 (lint: Assembly's source references no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block id). *Pillar:* P4. *Decides:* advisor R24, R29; LY-34.

**MSA-36 — Scope guards.** *Rule:* no hull-plate replacement (Interaction's FULL repair once the Graph rules, IDB Open Question 11), no seam repair (M7 on a SEAM is IDB Open Question 12; a seam is restored by a re-weld, never for free), no re-weld of a used socket, no discard, no unload, no rotation, mirror, free placement or resizing, no `remove_module`, no `q` upgrades or tool tiers, no cut as a weapon, no player-placed lamps. The only plate Assembly ever causes is the cap plate, which is Layout's presentation of `CAPPED`. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-58 (review). *Pillar:* anti-pillars. *Decides:* advisor R22.

**MSA-37 — Co-op seats `[VS-B]`.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the multi-seat rules below need a second seat and are out of the MVP gate; the per-seat data shape (a map keyed by PlayerId, ascending-PlayerId iteration, AC-MSA-07b) is still built in the MVP with one seat.)* *Rule:* up to four seats; each has its own channel record, `pending` and `last_result`. **The same socket gives `BUSY` at begin:** IA-34 makes contention one job per `(subject_ref, verb class)`, and WELD is a verb class, so a second seat's `begin_weld` on a socket already being welded is an immediate `BUSY`; two seats channelling the *same* socket cannot happen. Channels do not stack or shorten. **A double DONE is reachable only with two seats on the two different sockets of one pair** (MSA-11 lets either socket of the pair be focused, and IA-34's key is the focused subject, not the derived pair). Each pays its full `D` and both emit TOOL noise. If both reach DONE on the same tick, `assembly.step` submits two SYSTEM completions in ascending PlayerId order, the first applies, and the second's `validate` fails `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` (the pair's sockets are already `WELDED`), producing `NOT_TAKEN` for that seat (not an error, not a fault). If they reach DONE on consecutive ticks, the second seat's handoff pre-check fails first with `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` and `REJECTED` is written, or, if the first completion has been submitted but not yet applied, the second completion's `validate` fails and it resolves as `NOT_TAKEN`. **Two seats on the same seam cut:** the second `begin_seam_cut` is `BUSY` (IA-34, class WELD, ASK I1(iv)); on the two sockets of one pair the second completion fails `SEAM_NOT_ACTIVE` and resolves `NOT_TAKEN`. Optional ASK I1(x): key WELD contention on the *host socket of the derived pair*, which would turn the second-socket case into an immediate `BUSY` too and make the double-DONE case unreachable. `assembly.state` is replicated as `SHARED_SUMMARY`; a crewmate's weld in progress is visible through Interaction's replicated channel record (the human channel, P1). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-59 (auto: two seats, same tick and consecutive ticks, exactly one `DONE` and a single welded state). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* TD-12; IA-34.

**MSA-38 — Restore and pause.** *Rule:* a restore drops every channel (abort cause `RESTORE`, IA-36); `assembly.state` has nothing to clear, because `snapshot()` stores `pending` as NONE and `last_result` is runtime-only and so is empty after any restore (MSA-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; nothing is half-applied because the apply is atomic and a snapshot is taken only at a tick boundary. Completions are never replayed from a save. While the simulation is paused no tick advances (no P3, so no hook submits), the TTL and the ledger are in ticks and stop, and resume continues as if there had been no pause. For `persist` blocks, restore-then-continue equals uninterrupted play (kernel G4) at every tick where no ASSEMBLY channel record is open and no `pending` is set; the differences are asserted explicitly rather than hidden: while a channel is open the restore drops the channel record and its ledger entry (abort cause `RESTORE`, E-29), and while `pending` is set (from `submit_T` to the apply, or to the TTL, up to 13 ticks after a rejection, E-30, E-33) the completion is in the kernel queue, which no save holds, so the restore loses it (the **non-snapshot ticks**, MSA-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the permitted difference is exactly one key, and the test asserts that only it differs:** PD-1, the seat's ASSEMBLY channel record and its ledger entry in `interaction.state` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: PD-2, `seats[p].pending`, is deleted: `snapshot()` stores `pending` as NONE, MSA-4, so it never differs between a stored and a restored state)*. `last_result` is not a permitted difference because it is runtime-only and outside the hash (MSA-4). A completion that was queued but not applied is not in any block, so a restore drops it with the queue; the world then differs from the uninterrupted run after the dropped weld or cut, so the equivalence claim is made per snapshot tick: for every snapshot tick `s` at which PD-1 does not exist and no seat's live `pending` is set (a non-snapshot tick otherwise, MSA-4), restore-then-continue is hash-equal to the uninterrupted run at every tick `>= s`; for a snapshot tick `s` inside PD-1 or a non-snapshot tick, the claim is only that the restored state at `s` equals the uninterrupted state at `s` with exactly PD-1 removed (the stored `pending` is NONE in both), and the script then re-drives the verb from its `begin_*`. AC-MSA-61 and S7 assert it.)* *(orchestrator ruling, QA-lead flag F-1: the earlier wording "except the handoff-to-apply tick" was contradicted by E-29.)* *Criterion:* AC-MSA-60 (auto: restore mid-channel leaves no channel, a stored `pending` of NONE, no `last_result`, no orphan, no cue), AC-MSA-61 (auto: snapshot at every tick of a weld-and-cut script, restore, continue; hash-equal except the asserted window). *Pillar:* P1, P5. *Decides:* IA-36; SL-5; KRN G4.

**MSA-39 — No presentation work inside the sim apply; budgets are spike-measured.** *Rule:* a weld or cut apply marks dirty keys and returns. The PROJECTOR (Layout -> scene), the Emitter rebuild (EM-30), the Lighting partition and Failure & Trail rebuilds run as P5 subscribers after the commit with writes disabled; if several ticks run in one render frame (catch-up, `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` 4) they coalesce to the latest committed state and never replay each tick's change. Budget placeholders, all named in T9, measured in the spike and none a measured fact today: whole weld apply <= 0.5 ms Release (`MSA_WELD_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`; the Graph's M2 alone <= 0.2 ms is locked and sits inside it), whole cut apply <= 0.5 ms (`MSA_CUT_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`), install apply <= 0.2 ms (`MSA_INSTALL_APPLY_BUDGET_MS`), `assembly.step` idle <= 0.02 ms (`MSA_STEP_IDLE_BUDGET_MS`; it runs 60 times a second), P5 subscribers on the weld frame <= 8 ms (`MSA_WELD_FRAME_P5_BUDGET_MS`) with the PROJECTOR <= 4 ms (`PROJECTOR_WELD_BUDGET_MS`, `[UNV]`) and no frame above 33 ms (`WELD_FRAME_HITCH_MAX_MS`), and `weld_offer` per call <= `MSA_WELD_OFFER_BUDGET_US` (value set in the spike), since the Pipeline's camera cut hides a one-to-two-frame hitch. These are co-measured with Body's own weld-projection spike (its S3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **the first weld frame has two costs the budgets above do not cover.** (1) *First-use compile:* the first weld or cut frame is the first time the weld and cut sprites, the spark and bead materials and any shader variant they pull in are drawn, so a cold shader or pipeline compile can land on that frame. Rule: **the weld, cut and outcome-cue assets (bead pieces, hatch states, sputter, gutter, bump, spark and cursor materials) are preloaded at scene load, and a warm-up draw of each material runs behind the loading screen**, so that no pipeline compile happens on the weld frame. (2) *Event autosave:* the `ASSEMBLY_WELD` and `ASSEMBLY_CUT` events (MSA-33) ask Save/Load for a synchronous in-memory snapshot (kernel CR-18) that can land on the same frame as the P5 rebuild. Rule: Save/Load owns `event_due` and adopts no settle conjunct, so the event capture may share the weld frame; the capture is therefore INSIDE the measured hitch, and AC-MSA-63 and S3 measure the **whole frame** including a capture that fires on it (kept as written). The settle request to Save/Load is withdrawn *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1/G3)*. S3 is run on a cold cache, in an export build, not only in the editor, because editor numbers hide both costs.)* `assembly.step` and the completion payloads are pure functions of block state, so replay and MIRROR identity hold. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-62 (lint and auto: determinism of `assembly.step`; no wall-clock or RNG), AC-MSA-63 (spike: P5 subscriber cost and frame hitch). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* KRN CR-10, CR-17, H9, H10; TD-15.

**MSA-40 — Every invariant is stated for every reachable state, not just the default.** *Rule:* conservation (a weld adds edges only; a cut tombstones them; no node is minted), `abs(actor)` of every actor, offsets on the 24-px grid, and the body count hold at **every** reachable state: zoomed in and out on the integer ladder (`k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]`; nothing in these rules depends on zoom, and the in-world cursor scales with the world viewport while the prompt and bar keep their HUD pixel size), with a carried module, with zero to four seats, with a CASCADE stub submitter, after a restore, and in MIRROR. Tests assert `abs` and section-local position, never raw `pos_curr` (a weld followed by a cut is not an identity on `pos_curr`, BDY-23). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-64 (auto: the invariant matrix over those states). *Pillar:* P1. *Decides:* advisor R28.

**MSA-41 — The body count is bounded by construction; Assembly adds no capacity rule.** *Rule:* the number of live bodies satisfies `N(t) = N0 - W(t) + C(t)` with `C(t) <= W(t)` (every cut needs a prior ACTIVE weld), hence `N(t) <= N0` for every reachable sequence (formula D.8). MVP worst case: home + A + B + pod = 4 bodies before the weld, 3 after it, 4 after the one cut; the ceiling is one cut because both MVP sockets go terminal (LY-13). The lint `bodies_after_worst_sequence <= min(MAX_BODIES, BODIES_LIVE_MAX)` is 4 against `MAX_BODIES` 8 and the 2D Lighting placeholder `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` 4: **the equality is a risk, not a margin**; adding any body outside Assembly (a second pod, a loose piece Web Map keeps alive) or any Vertical Slice socket-economy change **degrades cross-body lighting: surplus bodies' lights are drawn as `OTHER_BODY` stand-ins (2D Lighting cross-body isolation rule)**. It is a degradation, not a fault: the sim is unaffected, but a body beyond the cap would lose real light cast onto its own geometry. ASK LT1 (T15) asks the 2D Lighting owner to confirm `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` 4 against this zero-margin worst case or to raise it to 5. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: **LT1 is closed, citing LO-24.** 2D Lighting's LO-24 and its Tuning Knobs row define a body as *live* when it is built and has a non-dormant section or hosts the avatar, state the MVP worst case as "exactly 4, zero margin accepted", and degrade any surplus body to `OTHER_BODY` stand-ins. The two documents' worst cases are reconciled in one line each: **LO-24:** live bodies at most 4, zero margin accepted; **WM-24:** at most one unwelded derelict is loaded and the pod's section is always dormant, so the bodies that are live at any moment are fewer than the bodies that are built (home, the berthed derelict, and the pod only while it hosts the avatar), which makes Assembly's count of built bodies (D.8: 4, then 3, then 4) the conservative bound. The assertion is **warn-only**: INV-6 (T7) raises the diagnostic `MSA_BODIES_LIVE_WARN` when `body_count` exceeds `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` and fails nothing; it is hard only at `MAX_BODIES` 8.)* `CAPACITY` on `can_detach` and a `MAX_SECTIONS_PER_BODY` value are deferred to Vertical Slice (Layout Open Question 8). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-65 (lint and auto: the worst MVP sequence ends at 4 bodies; the equality is reported as zero margin). *Pillar:* P5. *Decides:* advisor R7.

**MSA-42 — Do not fake a choice in the weld; the real decisions are whether, when and how clean.** *Rule:* the MVP weld is deliberately choiceless (MSA-13; Player Fantasy). The design commits to: no quality slider, no weld pattern, no rotation; the real decisions are **whether** to weld versus strip (neither line dominates; the playtest gate checks that both are taken), **when** relative to Attention, and **how clean** a later cut will be. Degenerate-play ledger, resolved: cancel-to-peek costs tool noise per accrued tick and the ledger is time-bounded (Interaction's); weld, strip by V8 salvage, cut away is an intended healthy line (each V8 costs noise and leaves open ends to cap, the cut is `LOUD`); weld-cut-weld to reset or farm is unreachable (terminal sockets, nothing minted); a RAGGED cut breaches both sides including the home side, so it is self-harm, never a weapon ("a cut never removes a threat the player is not leaving behind"); shedding an infested section after the seam has been prepared is healthy P5 play (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* it is a prepared amputation, not an escape; a cut made under attack is RAGGED and breaches home, so it is the worst way out), with the rule that **a cut must not launder Attention** (the locus falls back, the level does not reset: a verify handed to the Attention owner, ASK A1); battery-banking through weld and cut is not a faucet (conservation). **First-weld scaffold (authoring sequencing, no change to `weld_offer`):** before derelict B becomes dockable, the player has already exercised V4 and V3 on `home_ship` (clearing the home-ship faults), so the first connect is not a difficulty spike on a leaking seam; `weld_offer` never reads player history (ASK D1 answered by DA OQ-DA-31: no gate needed). *Criterion:* AC-MSA-66 (review: no choice-faking element exists), AC-MSA-131 (auto: no strip line makes `weld_join` permanently impossible; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*), AC-MSA-69 (manual: both the weld line and the strip line are taken by at least 2 of 5 playtesters), AC-MSA-70 (manual: median time from prompt-first-appears to channel-begin <= 45 s, and from bead to first seam-breaker close 60-180 s; both are `[PLACEHOLDER]` **playtest targets for the playtest gate, not sim knobs**, and live in the playtest script rather than in any data file). *Pillar:* P5, anti-pillar, SDT honesty. *Decides:* game-designer G1, G2, G13; advisor R11.

## Tuning Knobs

Every number below is data-driven (a data file, never hardcoded). Assembly owns few knobs on purpose: the Graph owns what a weld does to the world, Interaction what the channel costs the web, Layout where sockets sit. **★ marks a registry candidate** (a cross-system fact another GDD reads or must obey); every new name is `[PLACEHOLDER]` until the playtest gate or the spike sets it. Knobs owned elsewhere are in T18 with a pointer to their source of truth and are never restated with a new value (a different value is a CONFLICT, not a tweak here). Tick values are 60 per second; ticks that must span whole Graph blocks are multiples of `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6.

**T17 — Assembly-owned knobs.**

| Knob | Default | Unit | Safe range | Too high | Too low | Interacts with |

# TRs: Modular Ship Assembly (alias: assembly)

Source: design/gdd/modular-ship-assembly.md (Designed; MVP = weld + player seam cut + install; co-op `[VS-B]` and CASCADE `[VS]` excluded from MVP gate).

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-assembly-001 | Assembly registers exactly five command types (`begin_weld`, `begin_seam_cut`, `weld`, `seam_cut`, `install_module`) and no others (`remove_module` stays unregistered). | Core | MSA-1, T1 |
| TR-assembly-002 | `weld` and `seam_cut` are SYSTEM-origin only (allowed_origins = SYSTEM) with payload exactly `{actor, target, cause}` (no `q`, plan or mode), and their `max_age_ticks` equals `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` (8-119, default 12). | Core | MSA-6, T1, AC-MSA-09 |
| TR-assembly-003 | A weld/cut is two-phase: `begin_*` opens an Interaction channel and mutates no ship state; `assembly.step` hands off on DONE and submits the completion; the completion applies in P2 of the next tick (e.g. begin 437039 -> apply 437400 for D=360). | Threading/Timing | MSA-3, AC-MSA-04 |
| TR-assembly-004 | The same predicate body and reason order is evaluated at three sites (begin validate, handoff pre-check, completion validate), and the completion `validate` is the only authoritative site; declared skips are only those in T2a (e.g. `BUSY`, `NOT_DOCKED`, `CUT_STRANDS`). | Core | MSA-7, T2a, AC-MSA-10 |
| TR-assembly-005 | Every completion `apply` is atomic and no-rollback: it calls published mutators in fixed order (weld: Graph M2 -> Layout LM2 -> Body BM3 -> Interaction `sync_section` x2 -> `assembly.state`; cut: M3 -> LM3 -> BM4 -> `sync_section` x2 -> state), emits one P5 notification batch, and Body mutators never precede their Layout mutator (`BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`). | Core | MSA-14, MSA-20, T3, T4 |
| TR-assembly-006 | Assembly writes exactly one block (`assembly.state`); every other state change goes through a mutator published by the owning system (Graph, Layout, Body, Suit, Controller, Interaction). | Core | MSA-2, AC-MSA-03 |
| TR-assembly-007 | Every Class A mutator Assembly calls returns a status (`OK` or `FAULT_CODE`); `apply` checks it after every call, calls `ctx.fault(code, detail)` and returns `ctx.complete()` on first non-OK, and never relies on throw/assert (GDScript has none; assert is stripped in release). | Core | MSA-14, MSA-31, AC-MSA-142/143 |
| TR-assembly-008 | All kernel-invoked Assembly callables (`validate`, `apply`, `assembly.step`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`) take the kernel `ctx` and have `return ctx.complete()` as their only return statement. | Core | MSA-31 (callable contract) |
| TR-assembly-009 | A read-only cross-block verifier checks INV-1..INV-7 and INV-10: all eight hard in `post_restore` (restore fails to FAULTED on violation; INV-6 `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` half warn-only), and INV-1/2/4/5/7 after each weld/cut apply in release builds. | Core | MSA-32, T7, AC-MSA-52/53 |
| TR-assembly-010 | `assembly.step` is a hook (divisor 1, offset 0, after `interaction.step`) that reads only `assembly.state` and `channel_view`, iterates seats in ascending PlayerId, submits at most one SYSTEM command per seat per tick, and uses no wall-clock, RNG or dictionary-order dependence. | Threading/Timing | MSA-5, AC-MSA-07, AC-MSA-62 |
| TR-assembly-011 | `assembly.state` is a SIM block (`persist true`, scope WORLD, SHARED keyed by PlayerId, `SHARED_SUMMARY`, schema_version 1, `restore_after [layout.state, graph.state, interaction.state, body.state]`) holding per-seat `pending` and `last_result` plus the reserved CASCADE deferral record, and no channel progress or world history. | Save/Load | MSA-4, T6 |
| TR-assembly-012 | `snapshot()` writes every seat's `pending` as NONE (restore-idempotent, byte-identical re-snapshot) and `last_result` is runtime-only (outside snapshot, hashes and Save/Load payload); a save taken in the `pending` window (up to ~13 ticks) loses the in-flight completion, which is never replayed. | Save/Load | MSA-4, MSA-38, AC-MSA-05a/61/129 |
| TR-assembly-013 | 64-bit tick values (`T`, `submit_T`, `welded_at_T`) are stored as two 32-bit ints or strings and never as JSON numbers; the block uses no packed-array fields and dirty keys are marked explicitly in every mutator (Godot 4.7 packed-array element setter change). | Save/Load | MSA-4, MSA-31, AC-MSA-06 |
| TR-assembly-014 | Assembly publishes the pure read `last_shape_change_T()` (max of Layout `welds[].welded_at_T/cut_at_T`) for Save/Load to poll, event names `ASSEMBLY_WELD` / `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, and never calls Save/Load. | Save/Load | MSA-33, D.9, AC-MSA-54 |

## Consumes

- Command & Simulation Layer (kernel): `WriteScope`, `ctx` (`ok/reject/put/fault/complete`), CR-3 hook tuple, CR-4/5 command anatomy and `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)`, CR-9 no-rollback, CR-10 P5 batching, CR-19 FAULTED, `max_age_ticks`, `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`, `QUEUE_CAPACITY`, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`.
- Life-Support Graph: `can_join_static(plan)`, full `can_join(plan)` (with `surge[]`), `seam_view(seam_id)` (incl. `cut_sides`, `opening_ids[]`), `compartment(cid).band_p`, `check_install_module`; mutators M2 `weld_join` (returns `{seam_id, opening_ids[]}`), M3 `cut_detach(seam_id, boundary_mode)`, M5 `install_module(...)`; section `kind` HOME/DERELICT; `seam_at_weld`/`A_seam_m` formulas.
- Layout (`layout.state`): `socket_plan`, `can_attach`, `can_detach`, `detach_preview`, `subject_anchors`, `welds[]` reads; mutators LM2 `attach_section`, LM3 `detach_section`.
- Ship Body (`body.state`): `can_rebase_attach`, `can_rebase_detach`, `actors_overlapping(body_id, rects[])`, `docked(a, b, frame_shift_px)`, `body_count`, `actors_on`, `foot_boxes`; mutators BM3 `rebase_on_attach`, BM4 `rebase_on_detach`.
- Interaction: `open_channel(seat, owner_system, verb_id, target_ref, duration_ticks)`, `channel_view` DONE handoff, `sync_section`, channel clock/abort set/ledger/noise, declaration table rows (IA-23).
- Player Controller: `set_channel_ref(actor, ASSEMBLY, channel_id, face_octant)`, `clear_carry_ref(actor)`, PC-7/PC-8 carry carve-out.
- Suit & Equipment: `release_carried(player_id)`, tool slots (`tool_welder`, `tool_cutter`).
- Item DB: `compatible_defs(h)`, instance fields `def_id`, `condition_bp`, `cap_bp`, `patched_at_step`.
- Save/Load: polls Assembly's reads; Assembly never calls it (autosave interval/gap/max-defer knobs).
- Web Map & Transit: establishes `docked`, holds it while an ASSEMBLY channel is open (WM-22), owns discard/orphan.
- Sanity (`harm_eligible`, `[VS-B]`), Attention (no push), Perception Filter (truth-channel tags), Adaptive Audio, HUD, Debug Overlay, Derelict Authoring (socket pair/lanes/offset), 2D Lighting (`BODIES_LIVE_MAX`), Emitter/Pipeline (P5 subscribers).

## Engine risk

- Custom fixed-tick sim (`TICK_RATE` 60, `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` 4); when driven by the physics callback must equal `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` -- LOW/MEDIUM (project-level tick-driver ADR; Godot physics-tick API is old, but `max_physics_steps_per_frame` setting interaction should be verified on 4.7).
- Godot 4.7 packed-array element-write no longer calls the property setter (breaking-changes.md) -- HIGH (4.5-4.7); mitigated by no packed arrays in `assembly.state` and explicit dirty-key marking.
- GDScript has no exceptions and `assert()` is stripped in release exports -- LOW (old), but drives the explicit status/`ctx.fault` design. Custom `Logger` for script errors marked `[UNV]` on 4.7.2 -- HIGH/unverified, not relied on.
- 64-bit integers vs JSON numbers in save serialisation (SL-2) -- LOW.
- Preload + warm-up draw of weld/cut materials/shaders to avoid first-use pipeline compile hitch (release export, cold cache) -- MEDIUM (Godot 4.4+ shader/pipeline compile behaviour; 4.5 shader baker is HIGH if used).
- Body/PROJECTOR scene rebuild, 2D lighting partition by body, camera cut on `BODY_TRANSFER` (Node2D/Camera2D/Light2D) -- LOW (Rendering owned by other systems).
- Synchronous in-memory snapshot on weld frame (kernel CR-18) -- LOW.
- No SubViewport, TileMapLayer, Jolt, MultiplayerAPI or AudioServer use directly by Assembly (MIRROR `SHARED_SUMMARY` replication is `[VS-B]`) -- LOW.

# TRs: Modular Ship Assembly (alias: assembly)

Source: design/gdd/modular-ship-assembly.md (Designed; MVP = weld + player seam cut + install; co-op `[VS-B]` and CASCADE `[VS]` excluded from MVP gate).

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-assembly-001 | Assembly registers exactly five command types (`begin_weld`, `begin_seam_cut`, `weld`, `seam_cut`, `install_module`) and no others (`remove_module` stays unregistered). | Core | MSA-1, T1 |
| TR-assembly-002 | `weld` and `seam_cut` are SYSTEM-origin only (allowed_origins = SYSTEM) with payload exactly `{actor, target, cause}` (no `q`, plan or mode), and their `max_age_ticks` equals `PENDING_TTL_TICKS` (8-119, default 12). | Core | MSA-6, T1, AC-MSA-09 |
| TR-assembly-003 | A weld/cut is two-phase: `begin_*` opens an Interaction channel and mutates no ship state; `assembly.step` hands off on DONE and submits the completion; the completion applies in P2 of the next tick (e.g. begin 437039 -> apply 437400 for D=360). | Threading/Timing | MSA-3, AC-MSA-04 |
| TR-assembly-004 | The same predicate body and reason order is evaluated at three sites (begin validate, handoff pre-check, completion validate), and the completion `validate` is the only authoritative site; declared skips are only those in T2a (e.g. `BUSY`, `NOT_DOCKED`, `CUT_STRANDS`). | Core | MSA-7, T2a, AC-MSA-10 |
| TR-assembly-005 | Every completion `apply` is atomic and no-rollback: it calls published mutators in fixed order (weld: Graph M2 -> Layout LM2 -> Body BM3 -> Interaction `sync_section` x2 -> `assembly.state`; cut: M3 -> LM3 -> BM4 -> `sync_section` x2 -> state), emits one P5 notification batch, and Body mutators never precede their Layout mutator (`BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`). | Core | MSA-14, MSA-20, T3, T4 |
| TR-assembly-006 | Assembly writes exactly one block (`assembly.state`); every other state change goes through a mutator published by the owning system (Graph, Layout, Body, Suit, Controller, Interaction). | Core | MSA-2, AC-MSA-03 |
| TR-assembly-007 | Every Class A mutator Assembly calls returns a status (`OK` or `FAULT_CODE`); `apply` checks it after every call, calls `ctx.fault(code, detail)` and returns `ctx.complete()` on first non-OK, and never relies on throw/assert (GDScript has none; assert is stripped in release). | Core | MSA-14, MSA-31, AC-MSA-142/143 |
| TR-assembly-008 | All kernel-invoked Assembly callables (`validate`, `apply`, `assembly.step`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `default_state`, `read_view`) take the kernel `ctx` and have `return ctx.complete()` as their only return statement. | Core | MSA-31 (callable contract) |
| TR-assembly-009 | A read-only cross-block verifier checks INV-1..INV-7 and INV-10: all eight hard in `post_restore` (restore fails to FAULTED on violation; INV-6 `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` half warn-only), and INV-1/2/4/5/7 after each weld/cut apply in release builds. | Core | MSA-32, T7, AC-MSA-52/53 |
| TR-assembly-010 | `assembly.step` is a hook (divisor 1, offset 0, after `interaction.step`) that reads only `assembly.state` and `channel_view`, iterates seats in ascending PlayerId, submits at most one SYSTEM command per seat per tick, and uses no wall-clock, RNG or dictionary-order dependence. | Threading/Timing | MSA-5, AC-MSA-07, AC-MSA-62 |
| TR-assembly-011 | `assembly.state` is a SIM block (`persist true`, scope WORLD, SHARED keyed by PlayerId, `SHARED_SUMMARY`, schema_version 1, `restore_after [layout.state, graph.state, interaction.state, body.state]`) holding per-seat `pending` and `last_result` plus the reserved CASCADE deferral record, and no channel progress or world history. | Save/Load | MSA-4, T6 |
| TR-assembly-012 | `snapshot()` writes every seat's `pending` as NONE (restore-idempotent, byte-identical re-snapshot) and `last_result` is runtime-only (outside snapshot, hashes and Save/Load payload); a save taken in the `pending` window (up to ~13 ticks) loses the in-flight completion, which is never replayed. | Save/Load | MSA-4, MSA-38, AC-MSA-05a/61/129 |
| TR-assembly-013 | 64-bit tick values (`T`, `submit_T`, `welded_at_T`) are stored as two 32-bit ints or strings and never as JSON numbers; the block uses no packed-array fields and dirty keys are marked explicitly in every mutator (Godot 4.7 packed-array element setter change). | Save/Load | MSA-4, MSA-31, AC-MSA-06 |
| TR-assembly-014 | Assembly publishes the pure read `last_shape_change_T()` (max of Layout `welds[].welded_at_T/cut_at_T`) for Save/Load to poll, event names `ASSEMBLY_WELD` / `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, and never calls Save/Load. | Save/Load | MSA-33, D.9, AC-MSA-54 |

| TR-assembly-016 | Weld apply is integer arithmetic only: no RNG and no wall-clock inside any Assembly apply or hook (replay and MIRROR identity). | Threading/Timing | MSA-14, MSA-5, MSA-39 |
| TR-assembly-017 | Weld/cut channels live in `interaction.state` as IA-14 records with `owner_system = ASSEMBLY`; Assembly runs no clock of its own; durations are `WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS` 360 and `SECTION_CUT_CHANNEL_TICKS` 240 (data-driven, multiples of `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, range 240-480). | Threading/Timing | MSA-30, AC-MSA-49 |
